item.title: RTX lifts 2026 forecasts as aerospace, defense demand drives record backlog
item.description: RTX raised its full-year profit and revenue forecasts on Tuesday as sustained demand for commercial aerospace services and military programs pushed its backlog to a record $340 billion and lifted third-quarter results.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: RTX (RTX.N) raised its full-year profit and revenue forecasts on Tuesday as sustained demand for commercial aerospace services and military programs pushed its backlog to a record $340 billion and lifted third-quarter results. The maker of Pratt & Whitney engines and Raytheon missile systems now expects 2026 adjusted earnings per share of $7.65 to $7.75, up from its prior forecast of $7.10 to $7.25. It also raised its sales forecast range to $97 billion to $97.5 billion, from $95 billion to $96 billion. "Demand for our products remains robust with over $81 billion of new commercial and defense awards, resulting in a record backlog of $340 billion," CEO Chris Calio said. This adds to the strong performance streak of major US aerospace and defense contractors, supported by robust airline maintenance spending, growing demand for aircraft engines and parts and sustained military spending amid heightened geopolitical tensions. Quarterly revenue at Collins Aerospace rose 10% on a 23% jump in commercial original equipment sales, while revenue at Pratt & Whitney increased 10%, helped by a 21% rise in commercial aftermarket sales. Raytheon sales climbed 14%, driven by higher volume in naval programs and land and air defense systems, including Patriot, Standard Missile, and Tomahawk. For the quarter ended September 30, adjusted profit rose to $2.26 per share from $1.70 a year earlier, while sales increased 11% to $24.97 billion.

item.title: Qualcomm to cut jobs worldwide in performance-focused layoffs, internal memo shows
item.description: Qualcomm will cut jobs globally in a "performance-focused reduction" following its annual employee reviews, CEO Cristiano Amon told staff in a memo on Monday reviewed by Reuters, with notifications set to begin in November.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Soni, Jaspreet Singh
item.content:encoded: Qualcomm (QCOM.O) will cut jobs globally in a "performance-focused reduction" following its annual employee reviews, CEO Cristiano Amon told staff in a memo on Monday reviewed by Reuters, with notifications set to begin in November. The cuts are part of an effort to build "a stronger performance culture" and address situations where the company "has consistently fallen short of expectations," Amon said. The memo did not say how many jobs would be affected, and Reuters could not immediately determine the scale of the cuts. Qualcomm did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It had about 52,000 employees globally as of September last year, most of them full-time. Its financial year typically ends in late September. One of the world's biggest smartphone chipmakers, Qualcomm has been hit this year by a slump in consumer electronics sales as soaring memory prices weigh on demand in key markets. Its shares have risen just 1.5% in 2026, compared with gains of more than 12% for the benchmark S&P 500 (.SPX) and nearly 60% for the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (.SOX) . In its latest earnings report in late July, Qualcomm forecast quarterly profit below estimates and said revenue from Apple products would decline faster than expected, while signaling that growth in data-center and other non-handset businesses would more than offset the lost revenue by fiscal 2027. The company expects the majority of its chip sales to come from businesses other than smartphones in fiscal 2027 as it expands into the fast-growing AI data-center market. Amon said in the memo business priorities, organizational needs, skills and expertise would be considered in making the cuts. "As we have expanded the business, so have the competencies and skills we require," he wrote. "We must have the right people in the right roles so they can perform at their best and the company can continue to succeed."

item.title: China envia forças navais para monitorar navio de guerra dos EUA próximo a banco de areia disputado
item.description: As Forças Armadas da China informaram nesta terça-feira que enviaram forças para monitorar um navio de guerra dos EUA que entrou “ilegalmente” nas águas ao redor de um banco de areia disputado no Mar do Sul da China, enquanto, mais ao norte na mesma região, Taiwan relatou um impasse com uma embarcação chinesa.
item.dc:creator: Liz Lee, Ben Blanchard
item.content:encoded: As Forças Armadas da China informaram nesta terça-feira que enviaram forças para monitorar um navio de guerra dos EUA que entrou “ilegalmente” nas águas ao redor de um banco de areia disputado no Mar do Sul da China, enquanto, mais ao norte na mesma região, Taiwan relatou um impasse com uma embarcação chinesa. A China considera quase todo o Mar do Sul da China como seu território, apesar das reivindicações sobrepostas de Brunei, Malásia, Filipinas, Taiwan e Vietnã, sendo que as tensões recentes têm sido mais acentuadas entre Pequim e Manila. O Comando do Teatro Sul das Forças Armadas chinesas afirmou que o USS Charleston “invadiu ilegalmente” as águas adjacentes ao Banco de Sabina, nas Ilhas Spratly, sem a aprovação do governo chinês, na madrugada desta terça-feira. “A ação dos EUA viola os direitos soberanos e os interesses da China, compromete a segurança marítima e é prejudicial à paz e à estabilidade regionais”, afirmou em comunicado. “O lado norte-americano deve cessar imediatamente tais atividades.” A Marinha chinesa enviou forças para rastrear e monitorar o navio, acrescentou. A Marinha dos EUA não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário. Geralmente, ela se refere a tais missões como “operações de liberdade de navegação”, embora a última conhecida no Mar do Sul da China tenha ocorrido há mais de um ano. Um porta-voz militar das Filipinas afirmou que o navio norte-americano “não invadiu o ‘território chinês’”, acrescentando que nenhuma nação tem autoridade para exigir permissão prévia para o “trânsito legítimo por águas internacionais”. No mês passado, uma embarcação da Guarda Costeira da China colidiu com um barco filipino que realizava uma missão de reabastecimento perto do mesmo banco de areia, segundo a Guarda Costeira das Filipinas. A China atribuiu a culpa pela colisão ao lado filipino. China e as Filipinas, que tem um tratado de defesa mútua com os EUA, disputam a soberania sobre o Banco de Sabina e todo o arquipélago das Ilhas Spratly. CONFLITO NAS ILHAS PRATAS Em um incidente separado na terça-feira, na extremidade norte do Mar do Sul da China, a Guarda Costeira de Taiwan informou que um navio da Guarda Costeira chinesa havia entrado em águas restritas perto das Ilhas Pratas, controladas por Taiwan. A Guarda Costeira de Taiwan informou que seu navio “Taichung” foi enviado para afastar a embarcação chinesa, enquanto ambos os lados transmitiam mensagens um ao outro. O navio chinês transmitiu que “a chamada República da China não existe”, referindo-se ao nome oficial de Taiwan, enquanto o navio taiwanês respondeu que “a República da China, Taiwan, é um país soberano e independente”, informou a Guarda Costeira de Taiwan, acrescentando que o impasse continuava. O Escritório de Assuntos sobre Taiwan, da China, não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário. O escritório afirmou na semana passada que Taiwan deve “arcar com as consequências” do uso de um canhão de água pela Guarda Costeira contra um barco de pesca chinês perto das Ilhas Pratas. As Ilhas Pratas ficam aproximadamente entre o sul de Taiwan e Hong Kong, mas contam com pouca defesa, e a segurança é de responsabilidade da Guarda Costeira de Taiwan. A China também vem intensificando as atividades da guarda costeira ao redor de Taiwan, inclusive na costa leste da ilha, o que tem causado preocupação nas capitais ocidentais. A China considera Taiwan, governada democraticamente, como seu próprio território.

item.title: Halliburton tops third-quarter profit estimates on international oilfield demand
item.description: Halliburton topped Wall Street expectations for third-quarter profit on Tuesday, as higher demand for its oilfield equipment in Latin America helped offset muted activity in the Middle East due to prolonged conflict in the region.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Halliburton (HAL.N) topped Wall Street expectations for third-quarter profit on Tuesday, as higher demand for its oilfield equipment in Latin America helped offset muted activity in the Middle East due to prolonged conflict in the region. Shares of the company were up 6% in premarket trading. Revenue in Latin America increased nearly 12.6% to $1.1 billion. The US oilfield services provider posted an adjusted profit of 60 cents per share for the three months ended September 30, compared with analysts' average estimate of 58 cents, according to data compiled by LSEG. "We are another three months into one of the largest energy disruptions in history. I expect the work to restore production, rebuild inventories and strengthen energy security will drive multi-year demand growth for oilfield services," Halliburton CEO Jeff Miller said in a statement.

item.title: Amazon invertirá más de 16.000 millones de euros en Alemania el año que viene
item.description: Amazon anunció el martes que tiene previsto invertir más de 16.000 millones de euros (unos 18.000 millones de dólares) en Alemania en 2027, con el fin de ampliar sus negocios de computación en la nube, inteligencia artificial, Internet por satélite y medios de comunicación.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Amazon anunció el martes que tiene previsto invertir más de 16.000 millones de euros (unos 18.000 millones de dólares) en Alemania en 2027, con el fin de ampliar sus negocios de computación en la nube, inteligencia artificial, Internet por satélite y medios de comunicación. Esta inversión supone la última iniciativa del gigante del comercio electrónico para hacer crecer sus operaciones en Europa, en su carrera por ampliar la infraestructura en la nube en toda la región, en un contexto de creciente demanda de servicios de IA y de creciente competencia entre las empresas tecnológicas. Este paquete, anunciado en la cumbre "Invest in Germany" celebrada en Berlín, se suma a los más de 100.000 millones de euros que, según Amazon (AMZN.O) , ha invertido en el país desde 2010. La última inversión incluye 4.800 millones de euros para ampliar la región en la nube de Amazon Web Services en Fráncfort y la infraestructura de IA. También incluye nuevos proyectos logísticos que se espera que generen más de 3.000 puestos de trabajo, el desarrollo de la red de banda ancha por satélite Amazon Leo y nuevas producciones de Prime Video. Amazon también tiene previsto abrir un segundo laboratorio de investigación en robótica e IA en Berlín. El compromiso se suma a una inversión de 10.000 millones de euros anunciada en junio de 2024 para ampliar su infraestructura en la nube y su red logística en Alemania, incluidos 8.800 millones de euros destinados a los centros de datos de AWS. (1 dólar = 0,8911 euros)

item.title: Rasperia fordert 342 Millionen Euro von RBI-Tochter in Russland
item.description: Die russische Gesellschaft Rasperia legt im Streit um den Baukonzern Strabag nach und fordert 342 Millionen Euro von der russischen Tochter der Raiffeisen Bank International (RBI). Dies erklärte ein Sprecher der Bank am Dienstag. Die Causa soll noch am selben Tag vor einem Gericht in Kaliningrad verhandelt werden, wobei eine Entscheidung zugunsten von Rasperia erwartet wird. item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Die russische Gesellschaft Rasperia legt im Streit um den Baukonzern Strabag (STRV.VI) nach und fordert 342 Millionen Euro von der russischen Tochter der Raiffeisen Bank International (RBI) (RBIV.VI) . Dies erklärte ein Sprecher der Bank am Dienstag. Die Causa soll noch am selben Tag vor einem Gericht in Kaliningrad verhandelt werden, wobei eine Entscheidung zugunsten von Rasperia erwartet wird. Wer derzeit hinter Rasperia steht, ist unklar. Früher wurde die Gesellschaft dem sanktionierten russischen Oligarchen Oleg Deripaska zugerechnet. Der Schritt ist das jüngste Kapitel in dem Streit, der auf die Entmachtung Rasperias als Strabag-Kernaktionärin nach den EU-Sanktionen gegen Deripaska im Jahr 2022 folgte. Rasperia reagiert nun auf ein [USN:FWN45E0J5 TEXT:"Wiener Gerichtsurteil"] vom September, das der RBI 3,15 Milliarden Euro Schadenersatz zusprach. Sollte Rasperia bis Mittwoch um Mitternacht kein Rechtsmittel einlegen, wird das Urteil rechtskräftig. Die RBI will dann die Verwertung der eingefrorenen Vermögenswerte beantragen: 28,5 Millionen Strabag-Aktien, einbehaltene Dividenden sowie Gelder aus einer Kapitalherabsetzung aus dem Jahr 2024. Die nun in Russland geltend gemachte Forderung von 342 Millionen Euro setzt sich aus zwei Teilen zusammen. Die Hauptforderung von 300 Millionen Euro entspricht der Differenz zwischen der Wiener Klagesumme von 3,15 Milliarden Euro und einer von einem russischen Gericht festgelegten Obergrenze von 2,85 Milliarden Euro. Hinzu kommen 42 Millionen Euro an Gerichtsgebühren. Die RBI, die größte westliche Bank in Russland, will mit ihrer Klage in Wien den Schaden aus einem russischen Urteil vom April 2025 kompensieren, das ihre Russland-Tochter zu einer Zahlung von rund 2,4 Milliarden Euro an Rasperia verpflichtet hatte. Zugleich kann die Bank seit Jahren keine Dividenden aus ihrem Russland-Geschäft an die Konzernmutter ausschütten. Ein russisches Gericht hatte der Bank in weiterer Folge zwar Klagen außerhalb Russlands untersagt, gleichzeitig aber ausdrücklich eine Schadenersatzklage in Österreich bis zu einem Streitwert von 2,85 Milliarden Euro ohne Strafandrohung erlaubt. Die RBI sah das Risiko damit als begrenzt an und reichte in Wien eine Klage über 3,15 Milliarden Euro ein, um Zugriff auf die in Österreich eingefrorenen Vermögenswerte von Rasperia zu erhalten. Hintergrund des komplexen Streits ist die Entmachtung Rasperias als Strabag-Kernaktionärin. Nach dem russischen Angriff auf die Ukraine 2022 verhängte die EU Sanktionen gegen Deripaska. In der Folge wurde das Rasperia-Aktienpaket eingefroren und Dividendenzahlungen ausgesetzt. Schlussendlich verklagte Rasperia die Russland-Tochter der RBI und erhielt von russischen Gerichten den milliardenschweren Schadenersatz zugesprochen. Die Gegenklage der RBI in Wien stützt sich auf eine seit Juni 2024 geltende EU-Regelung, die Unternehmen die Durchsetzung von Ansprüchen gegen eingefrorene Vermögenswerte ermöglicht.

item.title: Prudential Financial to sell Brazil, Mexico units for $4 billion
item.description: Prudential Financial said on Tuesday it would sell its Brazil and Mexico units to French insurance group CNP Assurances Group for $4.03 billion in cash as the US insurer continues to simplify its business.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Prudential Financial (PRU.N) said on Tuesday it would sell its Brazil and Mexico units to French insurance group CNP Assurances Group for $4.03 billion in cash as the US insurer continues to simplify its business. "We remain focused on narrowing our geographic footprint and building a simpler, more focused Prudential," CEO Andy Sullivan said. The transaction is expected to close in the second half of 2027. Morgan Stanley served as financial adviser to Prudential, while Goldman Sachs advised CNP Assurances.

item.title: 3M lifts annual profit forecast on cost controls, price hikes
item.description: Industrial conglomerate 3M lifted its full-year profit forecast on Tuesday after cost-control initiatives and higher prices supported margins, while its safety and industrial business remained resilient.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Industrial conglomerate 3M (MMM.N) lifted its full-year profit forecast on Tuesday after cost-control initiatives and higher prices supported margins, while its safety and industrial business remained resilient. The company now expects full-year adjusted profit per share of between $9.10 and $9.15, compared with its prior forecast of $8.80 to $8.95. Shares of the company were up 2.7% before the bell. Robust industrial activity in the US as well as growing sales of chipmaking machines and materials have helped the company offset uneven demand in some end markets affected by inflationary pressures. Under CEO William Brown, the company has also focused on improving customer service and operational execution as it works to strengthen growth and profitability. Its consumer-facing businesses have continued to operate in a challenging spending environment, reflecting cautious discretionary purchases by customers. At the same time, higher energy costs have raised concerns about the potential impact on manufacturing activity and broader industrial demand. While demand from automotive and consumer electronics customers has remained subdued, growth tied to data centers and semiconductor-related markets has provided a bright spot for 3M's Transportation and Electronics business, helping cushion weakness in some of its traditional end markets. The Saint Paul, Minnesota-based company launched 87 new products in the third quarter. It expects to reach over 350 product launches by the end of this year. The Scotch-tape and Post-it maker reported adjusted quarterly revenue of $6.6 billion, up 4.2%. The company's quarterly adjusted profit came in at $2.50 per share, compared with $2.23 per share a year ago.

item.title: French bond yields near 24-year high as new protests loom
item.description: France's government bond yields climbed further on Tuesday after their biggest daily rise in nearly a month, with investors remaining cautious as protest groups announced a new round of demonstrations planned for Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Rebaudo
item.content:encoded: France's government bond yields climbed further on Tuesday after their biggest daily rise in nearly a month, with investors remaining cautious as protest groups announced a [USN:L6N4660DJ TEXT:"new round of demonstrations planned for Saturday"]. French bond prices, which move inversely to yields, slid on Monday after weekend protests led to riots across France, adding to the difficulties the government faces in reducing its large deficit. France's OAT yields were up 3 basis points (bps) at 4.96%; it reached 4.9937%, its highest since July 2002, in early October. The yield gap between OATs and Bunds widened by 5.5 bps to 152.50 bps. It reached 158.67 basis points in early October, the highest level since November 2011. The Italian spread also rose 4.5 bps to 113.51 bps. “While not pivotal to the overall process, today’s vote on the revenue side of the (French) budget bill takes on a little more importance as a near-term signal,” Jamie Searle, European rate strategist at Citi, said. French far-right leader Marine Le Pen and hard-left rival Jean-Luc Melenchon [USN:L8N4601WM TEXT:"extended their lead over other candidates"] in a poll published last week — before the weekend's events, a scenario analysts view as the least favourable for efforts to reduce France's fiscal deficit. "The protests highlight that any government will struggle to implement the required reforms and savings against broader public resistance," Benjamin Schroeder, senior rates strategist at ING, said. "The beneficiaries (of the protests' political fallout) appear to be the right and centre candidates, while on the far left, Melenchon’s chances of winning the presidential race have been pared back," he added, arguing that Melenchon’s plans are viewed as among the most controversial. Meanwhile, euro zone benchmark Bund yields edged lower but traded within their recent range after last week’s drop, as persistent energy price pressures kept investors from scaling back bets on further European Central Bank rate hikes. Oil prices advanced on Tuesday, with [USN:L1N46601X TEXT:"Brent hovering around a five-month high"]. Analysts said it will be difficult to materially reduce the market's bias towards further rate hikes, as a credible decline in energy prices remains elusive and winter weather is likely to play a crucial role in determining the path of gas prices. Germany’s 10-year government bond yields , the euro zone benchmark, were down 2 bps to 3.43%. They have moved between about 3.40% and 3.50% since early this month, barring last Thursday’s drop, when [USN:L6N4610C5 TEXT:"tech stocks took a beating"]. Germany's 2-year government bond yield , more sensitive to policy rate expectations, fell 1.5 bps to 3.07%.

item.title: Cloud, Raketen und Logistik: Amazon investiert Milliarden in Deutschland

Gleichzeitig baut Amazon seine Forschungskapazitäten für Künstliche Intelligenz (KI) und Robotik in Berlin aus. Weiteres Geld fließe in das Logistiknetzwerk des Online-Händlers sowie in die Produktion deutscher Shows, Filme und Serien für den Streamingdienst Amazon Prime Video.

item.title: Cobre opera en rango estrecho por incertidumbre sobre aranceles de EEUU
item.description: El cobre operaba con escasos cambios el martes, cotizando en un rango estrecho por tercera sesión consecutiva, ya que la incertidumbre sobre los posibles aranceles a las importaciones de Estados Unidos y las preocupaciones por la inflación impulsada por el aumento de los precios del petróleo mantenían moderado el apetito por el riesgo.
item.dc:creator: Polina Devitt
item.content:encoded: El cobre operaba con escasos cambios el martes, cotizando en un rango estrecho por tercera sesión consecutiva, ya que la incertidumbre sobre los posibles aranceles a las importaciones de Estados Unidos y las preocupaciones por la inflación impulsada por el aumento de los precios del petróleo mantenían moderado el apetito por el riesgo. * A las 0955 GMT, el contrato de referencia del cobre a tres meses en la Bolsa de Metales de Londres (LME) subía un 0,1%, a 14.353 dólares por tonelada. * El cobre, ampliamente utilizado en los sectores energético y de la construcción, ha ganado un 55% desde que Donald Trump volvió a la presidencia de Estados Unidos en enero de 2025, pese a que la demanda mundial ha caído un 0,5%, a 27 millones de toneladas, según señaló en una nota Tom Price, analista de Panmure Liberum. * Lo que respalda los precios es la escasez de chatarra de cobre en China, que está elevando su necesidad de cobre refinado debido a la reducción de las existencias nacionales, justo cuando Estados Unidos sigue importando metal y acumulando existencias ante la posibilidad de que se impongan aranceles, según Goldman Sachs. * Los analistas del banco prevén que los precios del cobre alcancen una media de 15.400 dólares en 2027, frente a los 14.700 dólares que se esperan para fines de 2026. * La prima del cobre Yangshan , un indicador clave de la demanda china de cobre importado, avanzó un 0,7%, a 138 dólares por tonelada, su nivel más alto en casi cuatro años. * Por su parte, las existencias de cobre en la bolsa Comex se situaban en un máximo histórico de 718.199 toneladas, frente a las 87.241 de enero de 2025. * En otros metales básicos, el aluminio bajaba un 0,8%, a 2.993 dólares la tonelada; el zinc perdía un 0,7%, a 3.688 dólares; el plomo operaba plano a 1.894,5 dólares; el estaño ganaba un 0,1%, a 50.775 dólares; y el níquel subía un 0,5%, a 15.600 dólares.

item.title: El Brent toca máximo de cinco meses, ataques a instalaciones saudíes avivan temores sobre suministro
item.description: Los precios del petróleo subían el martes, y el Brent tocó un máximo de cinco meses, ya que los operadores incorporaban en los precios una prima de riesgo geopolítico derivada de los ataques hutíes contra infraestructuras saudíes y de las noticias sobre ataques a buques en el golfo Pérsico.
item.dc:creator: Alex Lawler
item.content:encoded: Los precios del petróleo subían el martes, y el Brent tocó un máximo de cinco meses, ya que los operadores incorporaban en los precios una prima de riesgo geopolítico derivada de los ataques hutíes contra infraestructuras saudíes y de las noticias sobre ataques a buques en el golfo Pérsico. * Los hutíes de Yemen, alineados con Irán, dijeron el lunes que habían lanzado varios ataques contra objetivos energéticos, aeroportuarios y militares saudíes, como una planta de Aramco (2222.SE) en Yanbu, el yacimiento petrolero de Shaybah, el Aeropuerto Internacional Rey Jalid de Riad y el aeropuerto de Abha. * Las autoridades saudíes no confirmaron de inmediato las afirmaciones de los hutíes y Reuters no pudo verificarlas de forma independiente. * A las 1016 GMT, los futuros del crudo Brent cotizaban con un alza de 1,78 dólares, o un 1,62%, a 111,33 dólares por barril, su nivel más alto desde mayo. * El crudo estadounidense West Texas Intermediate (WTI) subía 4,49 dólares, o un 4,33%, a 108,15 dólares, su nivel más alto desde septiembre. * "Los precios del petróleo siguen contando con un buen respaldo... Esto sugiere que el mercado está descontando una prima de riesgo significativa, dada la volatilidad de la situación", señalaron los analistas de ING en una nota publicada el martes. * "Sin embargo, si los flujos continúan sin obstáculos a pesar del entorno geopolítico, es probable que la prima de riesgo se reduzca lentamente. Es evidente que, por el momento, no hay indicios de que esto vaya a suceder". * Al menos 18 buques fueron atacados en el transcurso de dos semanas, según reportes, lo que mantiene intacta la prima de riesgo, señaló el rastreador de buques Kpler en una nota el lunes. * También el lunes, un ataque hutí contra un campo de entrenamiento de las fuerzas de seguridad gubernamentales en la provincia yemení de Shabwa causó la muerte de 58 personas y dejó más de 200 heridos. * La reanudación de los ataques ha avivado los temores sobre la estabilidad regional y ha puesto de relieve los riesgos continuos para el suministro energético procedente de la región, lo que mantiene los precios del petróleo por encima de los 100 dólares el barril. * En Estados Unidos, los analistas esperaban que las reservas de crudo hubieran descendido la semana pasada, al igual que las de productos derivados, reveló el lunes un sondeo preliminar de Reuters.

item.title: Israeli fire kills four people in Gaza, medics say
item.description: Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least four Palestinians, including a married couple and a 17-year-old, in separate incidents in the Gaza Strip on Tuesday, health officials said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least four Palestinians, including a married couple and a 17-year-old, in separate incidents in the Gaza Strip on Tuesday, health officials said. Medics said an Israeli airstrike killed Akram Yassin and his wife Dina Abu Baker in an apartment in Gaza City. The Israeli military said it struck a militant in the area, without giving further details. In Khan Younis, in the south, medics said a 17-year-old boy was killed by Israeli gunfire near the Qizan Al-Najar neighbourhood, while another was killed by Israeli gunfire in the Zeitoun suburb east of Gaza City, taking Tuesday's death toll to at least four. The Israeli military did not immediately comment on either of the two gunfire incidents. Palestinians inspected the aftermath of the strike on the apartment in Gaza City before gathering for the couple's funeral. "We’re supposed to be in a ceasefire period, but honestly, we are not seeing a ceasefire or anything. The war is still going on, assassinations are continuing, and the shelling has not stopped," said Mahmoud Yassin, whose brother was killed. Israel, which says the Hamas militant group has been rearming and launching attacks in violation of the ceasefire, has stepped up strikes on the group in recent weeks. Hamas has denied trying to carry out attacks or rebuild its arsenal and accuses Israel of undermining the Gaza peace deal. The ceasefire, brokered by the US a year ago, calls for the eventual reconstruction of the territory. But little progress has been made towards implementing a deal to end the conflict that includes terms for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its troops. Gaza health officials have said at least 1,500 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli fire since the ceasefire. Israel says four of its soldiers have been killed by militants in Gaza over the same period.

item.title: UK to fly RAF missions defending Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks, Bloomberg reports
item.description: Britain will deploy Royal Air Force fighter jets on defensive missions to help protect Saudi Arabia from escalating Houthi attacks, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday, citing British officials familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain will deploy Royal Air Force fighter jets on defensive missions to help protect Saudi Arabia from escalating Houthi attacks, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday, citing British officials familiar with the matter. RAF Typhoon fighter jets will help defend Saudi cities and infrastructure against aerial attacks by the Iran-backed group, while Britain will also provide an Atlas A400M transport aircraft and military advisers, the report said. Britain's Ministry of Defence did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In September Britain said it would provide [USN:L8N45D1VG TEXT:"additional defensive military assistance"] to Saudi Arabia following renewed Houthi attacks, including an RAF Voyager air-to-air refuelling aircraft. That announcement did not include fighter jet support. Houthi attacks have intensified in Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, with Yemen authorities saying on Monday that a strike on a government security forces training camp had killed 58 people.

item.title: ABB verbucht Rekordaufträge dank Rechenzentren-Boom
item.description: Dank des Booms bei Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) brummen die Geschäfte des Elektrotechnikkonzerns ABB. Getrieben von der Nachfrage nach Ausrüstung für Rechenzentren verbuchte das Schweizer Unternehmen im dritten Quartal einen Rekord beim Auftragseingang, wie ABB am Dienstag mitteilte. Gleichzeitig kündigte der Siemens-Rivale ein neues Gemeinschaftsunternehmen mit der japanischen Mitsubishi Electric an. An der Börse geriet die ABB-Aktie wegen Zweifeln an der Nachhaltigkeit des weltweiten KI-Booms und eines hinter den Erwartungen zurückgebliebenen Gewinns dennoch unter Druck.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Dank des Booms bei Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) brummen die Geschäfte des Elektrotechnikkonzerns ABB (ABBN.S) . Getrieben von der Nachfrage nach Ausrüstung für Rechenzentren verbuchte das Schweizer Unternehmen im dritten Quartal einen Rekord beim Auftragseingang, wie ABB am Dienstag mitteilte. Gleichzeitig kündigte der Siemens (SIEGn.DE) -Rivale ein neues Gemeinschaftsunternehmen mit der japanischen Mitsubishi Electric (6503.T) an. An der Börse geriet die ABB-Aktie wegen Zweifeln an der Nachhaltigkeit des weltweiten KI-Booms und eines hinter den Erwartungen zurückgebliebenen Gewinns dennoch unter Druck. Von Juli bis September kletterte der Auftragseingang von ABB um 40 Prozent auf 12,1 Milliarden Dollar. Im profitabelsten Geschäftsbereich Elektrifizierung, der Ausrüstung für die Stromversorgung von Rechenzentren liefert, schossen die Bestellungen um 70 Prozent nach oben. Im Segment der Rechenzentren selbst gab es ein dreistelliges Plus. "Rechenzentren waren herausragend", erklärte Konzernchef Morten Wierod. Es gebe keine Anzeichen für eine nachlassende Nachfrage oder eine Zurückhaltung der Kunden bei den Investitionen. Der konzernweite Umsatz stieg um 14 Prozent auf 9,7 Milliarden Dollar, während sich die operative Gewinnspanne (Ebita) auf 20,8 Prozent verbesserte. ABB hob den Jahresausblick leicht an und peilt nun ein vergleichbares Umsatzwachstum im niedrigen zweistelligen Prozentbereich an. Wierod betonte, dass sich der Markt für den Bau von Rechenzentren weiter beschleunige. "Wir stehen erst ganz am Anfang der Einführung von Künstlicher Intelligenz, sowohl in der Industrie als auch bei Privatpersonen", sagte der Konzernchef. Dies werde die Entwicklung in den kommenden Jahren antreiben. Rechenzentren seien daher auf Jahre hinaus ein Wachstumsmarkt. "NACHLASSENDE KI-EUPHORIE" Um das Wachstum in Asien weiter anzukurbeln, gründet ABB ein Gemeinschaftsunternehmen mit Mitsubishi Electric (6503.T) . Für umgerechnet rund 495 Millionen Dollar erwirbt ABB eine Mehrheitsbeteiligung von 51 Prozent an dem ausgegliederten Produktgeschäft der Japaner für Niederspannungs-Energieverteilung. Zudem übernimmt ABB die Vertriebsaktivitäten außerhalb Japans komplett. Die Transaktion soll in der zweiten Jahreshälfte 2027 abgeschlossen werden. Mittelfristig besteht eine Option auf eine vollständige Übernahme. Wierod erklärte, Ziel sei es, damit zum Marktführer in Japan aufzusteigen und auch vom dortigen Ausbau der Rechenzentren zu profitieren. ABB-AKTIE UNTER DRUCK Trotz der starken operativen Zahlen verlor die ABB-Aktie an der Börse sechs Prozent an Wert. Saxo-Anlageexperte Erik Schafhauser wies darauf hin, dass das Management im vierten Quartal einen leichten Rückgang der operativen Marge gegenüber dem Vorquartal erwartet. Zudem habe der Gewinn je Aktie im dritten Quartal die Analysten-Erwartungen verfehlt. ABB begründete dies mit Sondereffekten wie einer Belastung für eine Absicherung gegen Wechselkursschwankungen im Zusammenhang mit der geplanten Übernahme des britischen Industrieausrüsters Rotork sowie Abschreibungen von 80 Millionen Dollar aus dem Verkauf des Robotikgeschäfts. Analyst Marco Estermann von der Luzerner Kantonalbank wies auf die nachlassende KI-Euphorie am Markt hin, die die vergleichsweise hohe Bewertung der ABB-Aktie auf die Probe stelle. "Auch andere europäische Unternehmen, die vom KI-Boom profitieren, stehen heute unter Druck. Dies deutet darauf hin, dass der Markt nach einer starken Kursrallye das kurzfristige Aufwärtspotenzial für Industrieunternehmen mit KI-Bezug neu bewertet", so Estermann. Anleger stellen zunehmend infrage, ob sich die gewaltigen Investitionen der Technologiekonzerne tatsächlich in absehbarer Zeit auszahlen werden. Diese Verunsicherung zeigte sich auch an den asiatischen Börsen, wo Halbleiter- und Rechenzentren-Titel aus den Depots der Anleger flogen. So brach die Aktie des südkoreanischen KI-Infrastrukturanbieters Elice Group (0158S0.KQ) bei ihrem Börsendebüt um fast 30 Prozent unter den Ausgabepreis ein. Zudem verschoben mehrere Rechenzentren-Firmen wie Firmus, AirTrunk und SB Energy zuletzt ihre Pläne für einen Börsengang.

item.title: El oro cae debido a que mayores precios del crudo avivan temores sobre inflación
item.description: El oro caía levemente el martes, debido a que el aumento de los precios del petróleo avivaba los temores sobre la inflación, mientras los inversores esperan la reunión de la Reserva Federal de la próxima semana en busca de pistas sobre las perspectivas de las tasas de interés en Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Vishak Mathew
item.content:encoded: El oro caía levemente el martes, debido a que el aumento de los precios del petróleo avivaba los temores sobre la inflación, mientras los inversores esperan la reunión de la Reserva Federal de la próxima semana en busca de pistas sobre las perspectivas de las tasas de interés en Estados Unidos. * El oro al contado bajaba un 0,5%, a 4.120,49 dólares por onza a las 0909 GMT. Los futuros del oro estadounidense con vencimiento en diciembre caían un 0,5%, a 4.139,10 dólares por onza. * "Las persistentes presiones inflacionarias, impulsadas por los elevados precios de la energía, siguen respaldando las expectativas de un mayor endurecimiento monetario por parte de la Reserva Federal", dijo Ricardo Evangelista, director y presidente ejecutivo de ActivTrades. * Los precios del petróleo subían el martes, con el Brent rondando su máximo de los últimos cinco meses, ya que los operadores descontaban una prima de riesgo geopolítico derivada de los ataques hutíes contra infraestructuras saudíes y de las noticias sobre ataques a buques en el golfo Pérsico. * "Se espera de forma generalizada que la Fed mantenga las tasas de interés sin cambios en octubre, por lo que la atención se centrará principalmente en sus indicaciones sobre una posible subida en diciembre", añadió Evangelista. * Los recientes comentarios de las autoridades de la Fed, que apuntan a que no hay mucha urgencia por un mayor endurecimiento de la política monetaria, han atenuado las expectativas de una subida de tasas en la reunión de política monetaria del banco central del 27 al 28 de octubre, pero los operadores ven un 90% de probabilidades de que se produzca un alza en diciembre, según la herramienta FedWatch de CME. * Aunque el oro se considera tradicionalmente una cobertura contra la inflación, el aumento de las tasas de interés merma su atractivo, ya que los inversores prefieren activos que rindan intereses. * El índice de gastos de consumo personal (PCE) de Estados Unidos, el indicador de inflación preferido por el banco central y que se publicará la próxima semana, también está en el punto de mira de los inversores en busca de pistas sobre las perspectivas de las tasas de interés. * Por otra parte, en Japón, el gobernador del banco central, Kazuo Ueda, dijo que la inflación subyacente estaba "bastante cerca" del objetivo del 2%, lo que apunta a un margen para nuevas subidas de tasas. * En cuanto a otros metales preciosos, la plata al contado subía un 0,2%, a 57,1931 dólares por onza; el platino caía un 0,1%, a 1.639,45 dólares por onza; y el paladio bajaba un 0,9%, a 1.110,06 dólares por onza.

item.title: GM's core profit rises 22% on strength of pickup-truck business
item.description: General Motors’ third-quarter results easily beat analyst expectations on the back of resolute shoppers who continue to spring for pricey pickups and SUVs.
item.dc:creator: Kalea Hall
item.content:encoded: General Motors’ (GM.N) third-quarter results easily beat analyst expectations on the back of resolute shoppers who continue to spring for pricey pickups and SUVs. The company on Tuesday said quarterly earnings before interest and tax, not including one-time items (adjusted EBIT) rose 22% from a year earlier, to $4.1 billion. That amounted to $3.70 per share, topping analyst expectations of $3.63, according to LSEG data. The automaker said it expected to end 2026 with adjusted EBIT in the range of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion, narrowed from previous guidance of $14 billion to $16 billion. The company said it remained confident despite inflationary pressures from higher logistics and energy costs, tariffs and other expenses. GM shares fell about 6% in premarket trading. The company said its board approved a multi-year, $20 billion stock buyback program. GM has bought back about $29.5 billion of its own shares since 2023, driving down its overall share count to help its per-share profit results. GM in the third quarter sold a higher mix of large pickup trucks and fewer electric vehicles, which helped the bottom line. The automaker has been pulling back on sales of EVs, which historically have lost money, following the Trump administration’s withdrawal of support for them. Revenue totaled $50 billion, up 2.9% from a year earlier. In North America, the company’s profit margin improved to 8.7%, from 6.2% a year earlier, despite a slight decline in quarterly sales. GM said "the path forward is more challenging," but reiterated that it expects next year's results to be better, assuming continued strong consumer demand and a moderating of cost pressures on commodities and logistics.

item.title: Morning Bid: Rain from the neocloud
item.description: After a week of street riots and protests in France, the country's stocks and bonds are on edge, even as curfews in parts of Paris overnight appear to have restored some calm.
item.dc:creator: Mike Dolan
item.content:encoded: After a week of street riots and protests in France, the country's stocks and bonds [USN:L6N4650CW TEXT:"are on edge"], even as [USN:FWN4630KA TEXT:"curfews"] in parts of Paris overnight appear to have restored some calm. Such unrest rarely hits macro markets for long, if at all, but these events come at a difficult moment for France. French bond markets have suffered more than those of other G7 countries in the global debt selloff in recent months, as the country struggles to pass a [USN:L8N44H1DA TEXT:"government budget"] just to keep a lid on ballooning deficits and faces presidential elections next April. The street unrest amplifies the sense of political stasis and may even drag on already downbeat French economic soundings as well. There's no money in the public purse to offer as a sop to the protests. French debt yields hit fresh 24-year highs on Monday and risk spreads versus Germany neared the peaks of the past month. French stocks [USN:L6N4650GG TEXT:"underperformed"], with banks at the sharp end, and they [USN:L4N466020 TEXT:"slipped again"] on Tuesday morning. There has been some minor contagion to other euro zone debt markets but the euro [USN:L6N46502R TEXT:"slipped"] only marginally on Monday and has firmed again since. Back on Wall Street, tech stocks [USN:L6N4650KA TEXT:"grabbed a toehold"] on Monday after a bruising week - with some recovery in chip and AI-related indexes, as Netflix and SpaceX top Tuesday's earnings calendar. But there was renewed selling of tech names in Asia overnight, with South Korea's chip-heavy KOSPI [USN:L4N466020 TEXT:"on the slide again"] and an IPO from local data center builder Elice [USN:P8N42A06D TEXT:"bombing 30%"] on its market debut. That refocuses attention on so-called "neocloud" companies at the heart of the AI buildout after US data center firm CoreWeave plummeted last week. Meantime, Brent crude oil prices continue to [USN:L4N46600B TEXT:"probe"] five-month highs above $111 per barrel on Middle East violence, while four-year highs for European natural gas prices on the darkening Ukraine conflict are adding to the French tensions across the region. US Treasury yields appear to be tracking nervy stock markets closely, pushing higher yesterday on the small bounce in tech and also eyeing edgy energy prices. CHART OF THE DAY President Donald Trump's approval rating [USN:L6N465159 TEXT:"fell to a record low"] of 31% in the latest Reuters/Ipsos opinion poll, ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. Some 68% of Americans disapprove of Trump's handling of the economy, according to the poll, including 37% of self-identified Republicans. item.title: Hasbro raises annual revenue forecast on strong demand for digital games
item.description: Hasbro raised annual revenue forecast on Tuesday, betting on strong demand for its digital games, including "Magic: The Gathering", ahead of the crucial holiday season.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hasbro (HAS.O) raised annual revenue forecast on Tuesday, betting on strong demand for its digital games, including "Magic: The Gathering", ahead of the crucial holiday season. The Play-Doh maker has posted consecutive gains in its digital gaming segment over the past seven quarters, while an increase in sales of collectibles linked to Marvel, K-Pop Demon Hunters and Transformers have boosted demand for traditional toys. Revenue in its Wizards of the Coast and Digital Gaming segment rose 31% during the third quarter, while consumer products segment was up 4% from a year ago. The company's shares were up 1% in premarket trading. The toymaker expects fiscal 2026 revenue to grow in the range of 7% to 9% on constant currency basis, compared with its prior forecast a 5% to 7% rise. Hasbro has benefited from its investments in digital gaming, product innovation in key franchises and strategic partnerships, while rival Mattel (MAT.O) has come under investor pressure to better monetize its intellectual property. Quarterly revenue of Hasbro stood at $1.60 billion, compared with analysts' average estimate of $1.48 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. Its quarterly adjusted operating profit was up 52% at $541 million, including about $55 million of tariff refunds.

item.title: KI-Zweifel lassen Anleger nicht los - Warten auf US-Bilanzen
item.description: Sorgen über die weitere Entwicklung im Technologiesektor haben die Anleger an den Börsen weiter auf Trab gehalten. item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Sorgen über die weitere Entwicklung im Technologiesektor haben die Anleger an den Börsen weiter auf Trab gehalten. Der Dax (.GDAXI) und der EuroStoxx50 (.STOXX50E) notierten am Dienstagvormittag jeweils rund ein Prozent tiefer bei 25.090 und 6088 Punkten. Für schlechte Stimmung sorgten vor allem Rückgänge um knapp drei bis fast vier Prozent bei Unternehmen wie Infineon (IFXGn.DE) , Aixtron (AIXGn.DE) und Suss Microtec (SMHNn.DE) . "Die Sorgen um die hohen Bewertungen und die Finanzierung des KI-Booms nehmen weiter zu", sagte Andreas Lipkow, Chefanalyst beim Broker CMC Markets. Der europäische Technologie-Branchenindex (.SX8P) bröckelte um 1,5 Prozent ab. Eine milliardenschwere [USN:L8N4660FZ TEXT:"Kapitalerhöhung"] beim französischen Elektrotechnikkonzern Schneider Electric (SCHN.PA) drückte die Aktien um 3,5 Prozent ins Minus. In Zürich verlor ABB (ABBN.S) rund sechs Prozent, obwohl der Technologiekonzern einen [USN:L8N466062 TEXT:"Rekordauftragseingang"] dank der Nachfrage von Rechenzentren gemeldet hatte. Der Future für den Index der US-Technologiebörse Nasdaq gab ebenfalls erneut leicht nach. BILANZEN ALS ZÜNGLEIN AN DER WAAGE Auch an den asiatischen Börsen gerieten Unternehmen aus den Bereichen Halbleiter und Rechenzentren am Dienstag unter Verkaufsdruck. "Die Anleger stellen zunehmend infrage, ob sich die gewaltigen Investitionen der großen Technologiekonzerne tatsächlich in absehbarer Zeit auszahlen können", sagte Lipkow. Zusätzlichen Gegenwind für den Dax lieferten die höher als erwartet ausgefallenen deutschen [USN:L8N46512M TEXT:"Erzeugerpreise"] für September. In den Fokus der Anleger rückt die Bilanzsaison der Unternehmen. "Für eine Stimmungswende dürften vor allem die Ausblicke entscheidend sein: Überzeugende Wachstumsperspektiven und belastbare Gewinne könnten das Vertrauen stärken", sagte Salah-Eddine Bouhmidi vom Broker IG. Mit Blick auf die KI-Sorgen steht dabei die Geschäftsentwicklung von US-Technologieriesen wie SpaceX (SPCX.O) , Meta (META.O) und Tesla (TSLA.O) im Mittelpunkt. In Deutschland warten Anleger auf die Zahlen des Dax-Schwergewichts SAP (SAPG.DE) am Mittwoch. Bereits am Dienstag sorgten Geschäftszahlen kleinerer Unternehmen für Bewegung. Die Aktien von OVHcloud (OVH.PA) sprangen um 8,5 Prozent in die Höhe. Der französische Cloud-Anbieter wies für das bis Ende August laufende Geschäftsjahr erstmals seit seinem Börsengang 2021 einen positiven freien Barmittelzufluss (Levered Free Cash Flow) aus. Dagegen brachen die Papiere der auf Visualisierungstechnologie spezialisierten belgischen Firma Barco (BAR.BR) um 12,9 Prozent ein. Barco prognostizierte für das Gesamtjahr einen Umsatz leicht unter dem Vorjahresniveau. ÖLPREISE LEGEN ERNEUT ZU Ein erneuter Anstieg beim Ölpreis drückte zudem auf die Stimmung. Der Preis für Nordsee-Rohöl der Sorte Brent stieg um bis zu 1,4 Prozent auf 111,05 Dollar je Fass (159 Liter) und baute damit sein Fünfmonatshoch aus. Händler verwiesen auf einen Risikoaufschlag wegen anhaltender geopolitischer Gefahren, nachdem die vom Iran unterstützten Huthi-Milizen im Jemen zum Wochenstart [USN:L8N4651BG TEXT:"Angriffe"] auf Ziele in Saudi-Arabien gemeldet hatten. Bereits am Montag waren die Ölpreise gestiegen. Höhere Energiepreise schüren die Erwartung, dass die US-Notenbank die Zinsen zur Eindämmung der Inflation länger auf hohem Niveau belassen könnte.

item.title: GE Aerospace raises 2026 profit forecast as services strength drives growth
item.description: GE Aerospace on Tuesday raised its 2026 profit forecast for the second time this year, betting strong demand for engine maintenance and spare parts will offset the impact of higher fuel costs on flights.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: GE Aerospace (GE.N) on Tuesday raised its 2026 profit forecast for the second time this year, betting strong demand for engine maintenance and spare parts will offset the impact of higher fuel costs on flights. Airlines worldwide are cutting costs and capacity to defend ticket prices after the war in Iran disrupted oil shipping routes, driving up jet fuel costs and adding to pressure on the industry. With no end to the war in sight, higher fuel prices are testing airlines' ability to maintain schedules and margins, raising the risk of fewer flights and weaker demand for maintenance. GE Aerospace has said, however, that any impact on services revenue and profit this year should be limited, as much of its 2026 engine shop-visit work is already under contract and demand for spare parts continues to outstrip supply. Last month, GE Aerospace finance chief Rahul Ghai said the company had seen no changes to airlines' fleet plans, while the number of parked aircraft remained low. The jet-engine maker now expects 2026 adjusted earnings of $8.00 to $8.10 per share, up from its prior forecast of $7.65 to $7.85, and above analysts' consensus estimate of $7.92, according to data compiled by LSEG. "We are raising our 2026 guidance across the board, and we now expect 2027 commercial services to grow low-double-digits supported by our over $170 billion commercial services backlog," CEO Larry Culp said in a statement. Through CFM International, its joint venture with France's Safran, GE Aerospace is a leading supplier of engines for narrowbody jets and a major player in the widebody market. Parts and services account for more than 70% of its commercial engine revenue. Quarterly revenue at its commercial engines and services unit climbed 21% to $10.34 billion, driven by strong demand for aftermarket services. The company also raised its 2026 revenue growth forecast for the segment to the low 20% range, compared with its previous expectation of about 20% growth. It reported an adjusted profit of $2.25 per share for the quarter through September, beating Wall Street expectations of $2.01. Shares of the company rose nearly 1.2% in premarket trading.

item.content:encoded: Finanzexperten blicken erstmals seit Monaten pessimistischer auf die deutsche Wirtschaft. Das Barometer der Konjunkturerwartungen für die kommenden sechs Monate fiel im Oktober um 6,6 Zähler auf 28,1 Punkte. Das ist der erste Rückgang nach zuvor fünf Anstiegen in Folge, wie das Mannheimer Zentrum für Europäische Wirtschaftsforschung (ZEW) am Dienstag zu seiner monatlichen Umfrage unter 178 Investoren und Analysten mitteilte. Von der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters befragte Ökonomen hatten nur mit einem Rückgang auf 30,0 Punkte gerechnet. Zugleich schätzten die Experten die aktuelle Lage so gut ein wie seit über drei Jahren nicht mehr. "Die deutsche Wirtschaft kommt langsam aus der Stagnation heraus, doch der Aufschwung trägt sich nicht selbst", kommentierte ZEW-Präsident Achim Wambach die Entwicklung. "Privater Konsum und private Investitionen bleiben schwach, weil hohe Energiepreise die Realeinkommen drücken, die Produktionskosten erhöhen und die Inflation länger auf einem höheren Niveau halten." HOHE ZINSEN, NIEDRIGE PEGELSTÄNDE Banken-Ökonomen verweisen zudem auf gestiegene Kapitalmarktzinsen. "Langfristige Finanzierungen verteuerten sich, was auch der Unternehmenssektor zu spüren bekommt", sagte der Chefvolkswirt der VP Bank, Thomas Gitzel. "Und nicht zu vergessen sei auch, dass die niedrigen Pegelstände auf den deutschen Flüssen, zu einer Unterbrechung von Lieferketten führt", nannte Gitzel eine weitere Hürde für eine durchgreifende Erholung. Rekordvolle Auftragsbücher in der Industrie dürften dagegen die Konjunktur stützen. Dennoch dürfte das Wachstumstempo im zweiten Halbjahr wohl geringer ausfallen als im ersten, sagte der Chefvolkswirt der Privatbank Bethmann HAL, Alexander Krüger: "Es bleibt vorerst bei einer durch die Fiskalpolitik künstlich angetriebenen Konjunkturerholung." Für eine dynamische Konjunkturwende bedürfe es vor allem den Willen zu Strukturreformen. Europas größte Volkswirtschaft ist zuletzt drei Quartale in Folge gewachsen, angekurbelt vor allem durch die Exporte und staatliche Investitionen. Die Bundesregierung und die führenden Wirtschaftsforschungsinstitute haben deshalb ihre Wachstumsprognose für dieses Jahr auf 1,3 Prozent heraufgesetzt, nachdem im Frühjahr nur ein Plus von etwa einem halben Prozent erwartet worden war. Ein Problem bleibt die hohe Teuerung. Die Bundesbank rechnet für die kommenden Monate mit einem anhaltend hohen Preisdruck. "Derzeit ist davon auszugehen, dass die Inflationsrate in Deutschland bis ins nächste Jahr hinein merklich erhöht bleibt", heißt es im aktuellen Monatsbericht. Die Rückkehr zur angestrebten Zwei-Prozent-Marke werde "einige Zeit in Anspruch nehmen". Rekordhohe Preise für Benzin und Diesel sowie teures Heizöl haben die Verbraucherpreise im September mit 3,3 Prozent so stark steigen lassen wie seit knapp drei Jahren nicht mehr.

item.content:encoded: Wales have named uncapped trio Rhys Barratt, Aneurin Owen and Che Hope in their 39-player squad for November's home Nations Championship fixtures, while there are also recalls for Taine Basham, Seb Davies and Rio Dyer. Wales face Japan on November 7, before fixtures against New Zealand and Australia on consecutive weekends after that. Prop Barratt, centre Owen and scrumhalf Hope have all been called up and could earn a first cap as coach Steve Tandy looks at his options ahead of next year's Six Nations Championship. Tandy has left out experienced loose forwards Taulupe Faletau and Tommy Reffell, as well as centre Macs Page. The return of Basham, Davies and Dyer adds experience to the group, which is otherwise much the same as the one that did duty in July's Nations Championship fixtures. Wales beat Fiji but lost to Argentina and South Africa in their three games in the competition so far. item.title: Drug developer Lycia Therapeutics targets $938 million valuation in US IPO

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Drug developer Lycia Therapeutics said on Tuesday it was targeting a valuation of up to $937.7 million in its US initial public offering, as biotech companies flock to the IPO market. The South San Francisco, California-based company is seeking to raise up to $264.6 million in the IPO by offering 14.7 million shares priced between $16 and $18 apiece. The healthcare sector has anchored the fall IPO window this year in an otherwise lackluster market as investors become selective in a higher rate environment. Drug developers City Therapeutics (CTY.O) and Nvidia-backed Iambic Therapeutics (IAM.O) went public in New York last week. Jefferies, TD Cowen, Evercore ISI, and Guggenheim Securities are joint book-running managers. Lycia will list on the Nasdaq under the symbol “LYCA”.

item.title: Iran prolongs talks in stalemate to influence US midterms, officials say
item.description: Iran has deliberately prolonged talks with the US to try to weaken Donald Trump politically, while fears of renewed military action and deep distrust of Washington have reinforced Tehran's reluctance to strike a quick deal to end the war.
item.dc:creator: Parisa Hafezi
item.content:encoded: Iran has deliberately prolonged talks with the US to try to weaken Donald Trump politically ahead of November's [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"US midterm elections"], senior officials say, while fears of renewed military action and deep distrust of Washington have reinforced Tehran's reluctance to strike a quick deal to end the war. Three senior Iranian officials and an Iranian insider, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Tehran was convinced the US president was ready to resort to renewed attacks to try to break the stalemate in the eight-month-old war . "Iran is preparing for renewed Israeli and US attacks, not for a deal with America to end the war," one of the officials said. "The clerical establishment is determined not to give Trump a political victory." Tehran analyst Saeed Leylaz said that, by prolonging the talks, "Iran is influencing the US election without taking any unlawful action". IRAN CAN EXPLOIT TRUMP'S POLITICAL PROBLEMS The war, which began in February when the US and its ally Israel launched strikes on Iran, has helped drive Trump’s approval rating to a [USN:L6N46517O TEXT:"record low"] as polls suggest that Americans worried about high gasoline prices will punish his Republican Party in the November 3 congressional elections . Trump has repeatedly said he expects oil prices to drop after the elections, but has not offered a detailed plan to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy shipping route effectively closed by Iran since the war began. [USN:L1N45U0E0 TEXT:"Iranian attacks"] both threatened and real have kept ship traffic through the strait to a trickle, while a US maritime blockade and [USN:L1N45N0UK TEXT:"trade sanctions"] have cut off Iran's oil export revenues and exacerbated growing domestic [USN:L6N45K0UX TEXT:"economic woes"]. With Tehran refusing to make concessions it believes could benefit Trump politically, there is little chance of a breakthrough before the elections, the officials said. Under pressure from Israel, Washington wants Iran’s decades-long nuclear programme - which Iran says is purely peaceful and Western powers allege has military dimensions - on the table from the outset. For its part, Tehran insists that its conditions under a "seven-day plan" must be met before nuclear negotiations begin. And it offers no prospect of giving up the leverage over the Strait of Hormuz that the conflict prompted it to seize. Iran's Foreign Ministry and the US White House did not respond to Reuters requests for comment. IRAN CANNOT TRUST WASHINGTON, OFFICIALS SAY Iran’s proposal, conveyed through Qatari mediators, offered to reopen the strait within seven days, albeit under Iranian control, provided that Washington lifted its maritime blockade, eased restrictions on Iranian oil exports, released frozen assets and ended hostilities on all fronts. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on Sunday that the offer remained on the table, with messages being exchanged through mediators. Tehran's view that Washington cannot be trusted to commit to diplomacy stems from the attacks on Iran that have derailed previous negotiations, one Iranian official said. In June 2025, an Israeli attack wrecked plans for a sixth round of US-Iran nuclear talks in Oman. And last February, the US and Israel launched their war just after another round of talks ended, with further technical discussions scheduled. Maintaining a state somewhere between war and peace through the US midterms allows Iran to sustain pressure on Washington while reiterating its commitment to diplomacy. Trump has said the US will not bomb Iran again before November 3. However, the officials said Tehran continues to expect that bombing will resume, sooner or later. Alex Vatanka, director of the Iran program at the Middle East Institute in Washington, said the clerical establishment clearly wanted to hurt Trump politically. "But the fundamental issue is that Tehran believes that Trump is interested in regime change ... and following Israeli Prime Minister (Benjamin) Netanyahu’s policy of seeking to bring down Iran’s ruling establishment," he said. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth discussed Iran with Netanyahu on Monday, three Israeli officials said, in an unannounced visit to Israel a week before a parliamentary election in which Netanyahu's position is at risk. RETURN TO PREWAR STATUS IMPOSSIBLE FOR IRAN, SAYS ANALYST Iran’s strategy of keeping negotiations alive without rushing towards agreement comes at a cost. Prolonged uncertainty is weighing on Iran’s already crippled economy and wearing down public patience. Thousands were killed at the turn of the year when the security forces crushed spiralling anti-government protests. Annual inflation hit 73.6% in September, according to the Statistical Centre of Iran, and the rial currency has fallen nearly 35% against the dollar since Washington reapplied its naval blockade in July. Iran’s seaborne crude exports fell to zero in the second week of September from a 14-day average of 230,000 barrels per day at the start of the month, and remained there as of October 5, according to energy intelligence platform Vortexa. But the leadership's distrust of Washington extends beyond the current conflict to existential concerns. Iran believes the US has repeatedly broken agreements even when Tehran honoured its commitments, Leylaz said, leaving little confidence that any comprehensive deal would endure. “Reaching a sustainable deal with the US, even after the Trump administration, is no longer possible because of the deepened distrust,” Leylaz said. "Nothing will go back to the pre-war status quo."

item.title: Germany's far-right AfD investigates publication of emails stolen in cyberattack
item.description: Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) said on Tuesday that it was investigating the online publication of emails stolen by unknown hackers during a cyberattack last month.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) said on Tuesday that it was investigating the online publication of emails stolen by unknown hackers during a cyberattack last month. An AfD spokesperson said hackers had targeted a hosting service provider used by the party and apparently copied data from a small number of email accounts, most of which had not been used for years. "The recent online publication of what is presumably a portion of this data is currently being investigated," the spokesperson said. "A preliminary assessment can only be provided once this investigation has been concluded." The spokesperson did not say how much data was stolen. The statement followed a report by Bild newspaper saying over 420,000 emails linked to the party had been published online. According to Bild, the material included emails sent by party figures such as co-leader Alice Weidel as well as bank statements, academic certificates and membership lists. The website hosting the material was offline by Tuesday afternoon, but archived versions showed a trove of 281 gigabytes of data under the headline "The party's own records, unedited". The leak comes as the AfD, which has topped national opinion polls and made gains in recent state elections, faces calls from some politicians and civil society groups for it to be banned. They argue the party threatens Germany's democratic constitutional order, an accusation the AfD rejects as politically motivated.
