item.title: Nasdaq futures dip as oil prices climb, earnings loom
item.description: Nasdaq 100 futures slipped on Tuesday, pressured by renewed weakness in AI-linked stocks and a rebound in oil prices, as investors braced for earnings from major technology companies.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nasdaq 100 futures slipped on Tuesday, pressured by renewed weakness in AI-linked stocks and a rebound in oil prices, as investors braced for earnings from major technology companies. CoreWeave (CRWV.O) dropped 3.1% and Nebius Group (NBIS.O) lost 2.9% in premarket trading, while Apple (AAPL.O) fell 1% and Nvidia (NVDA.O) slipped marginally. The declines followed a brief reprieve on Monday, when the S&P 500 (.SPX) and Nasdaq (.IXIC) advanced as investors bought back into technology stocks following last week's sharp selloff, driven in part by concerns over CoreWeave's debt load and the cost of financing the AI buildout. "I see this as a dip inside a selective market rather than a genuine AI buying opportunity or the start of a deeper repricing," said Ion Jauregui, analyst at ActivTrades. "Investors are pickier about AI stories than they were a year ago." Elsewhere, shares of South Korean AI infrastructure company Elice Group (0158S0.KQ) tumbled nearly 30% in their market debut, slipping below their IPO price after the company raised 201.1 billion won ($151.12 million) in its offering. At 05:20 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were up 115 points, or 0.22%, S&P 500 E-minis were down 6.75 points, or 0.09%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis were down 147.75 points, or 0.5%. Brent crude was up 1.7% at around $111 a barrel, near a five-month high, as traders priced in a geopolitical risk premium from Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf. Investors will now watch this week's corporate earnings for clues on whether technology companies can maintain strong growth in the face of mounting macroeconomic risks. Quarterly results from SpaceX (SPCX.O) and Netflix (NFLX.O) are due after the market close on Tuesday, while heavyweights Meta Platforms (META.O) and Tesla (TSLA.O) are scheduled to report on Wednesday. General Motors (GM.N) , Hasbro (HAS.O) , Halliburton (HAL.N) , and 3M (MMM.N) are among the companies due to report before markets open on Tuesday. 3M (MMM.N) shares rose 3.9% after the [USN:L4N4651MW TEXT:"industrial conglomerate said"] it was expanding its commercial relationship with Amazon (AMZN.O) and had issued a warrant to an Amazon subsidiary, allowing it the right to buy 3M common stock worth over $521 million. Steel Dynamics (STLD.O) fell 6.3% after the [USN:L4N4651KV TEXT:"steelmaker missed"] third-quarter profit estimates.

item.title: Northrop lifts 2026 profit forecast on strong defense demand, record backlog
item.description: Northrop Grumman raised its annual profit forecast on Tuesday after strong demand for military aircraft, missile and defense programs helped beat Wall Street estimates for third-quarter profit, and drove its backlog to a record high.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Northrop Grumman (NOC.N) raised its annual profit forecast on Tuesday after strong demand for military aircraft, missile and defense programs helped beat Wall Street estimates for third-quarter profit, and drove its backlog to a record high. Shares of the West Falls Church, Virginia-based defense contractor rose nearly 2% before the bell. Northrop, which makes the B-21 Raider bomber and parts for the F-35 fighter jets, has been benefiting from rising US and allied military spending amid heightened geopolitical tensions. "I'm confident our new record backlog, well-positioned portfolio and investments, and industry-leading performance will continue to drive sales and earnings growth as reflected in our 2027 outlook," said CEO Kathy Warden. The company secured $16.4 billion in new contracts during the quarter, with its orders growing at 1.5 times its billings, driven by strong demand across programs including Sentinel, the F-35, Virginia-class submarines and certain classified programs. Northrop's backlog rose to a record $109.6 billion as of September 30. It now sees full-year 2026 adjusted profit per share in the range of $29.35 to $29.75, compared with its prior forecast if between $28.60 and $29.10. Quarterly sales rose 7% from a year ago to $11.12 billion on higher sales across all four sectors. Analysts expected $11.14 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. This growth was mainly driven by a 14% increase at its Aeronautics Systems unit, which benefited from increased B-21 bomber sales, higher F-35 production and sustainment work. Sales at its Defense Systems segment increased 12%, boosted by the continued ramp-up of the Sentinel missile program. Its quarterly profit came in at $7.89 per share, compared with analysts' estimate of $7.18 per share.

item.title: El Kremlin dice que espera que la reunión entre Putin y Witkoff sobre Ucrania pueda organizarse pronto
item.description: El Kremlin dijo el martes que esperaba que se pudiera organizar en un futuro próximo una reunión en Rusia entre el presidente Vladimir Putin y el enviado especial de Estados Unidos, Steve Witkoff, para debatir el proceso de paz en Ucrania.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Kremlin dijo el martes que esperaba que se pudiera organizar en un futuro próximo una reunión en Rusia entre el presidente Vladimir Putin y el enviado especial de Estados Unidos, Steve Witkoff, para debatir el proceso de paz en Ucrania. Se espera que Witkoff mantenga conversaciones este martes en Oslo con el presidente ucraniano, Volodímir Zelenski, y con representantes del E4, integrado por Reino Unido, Francia, Alemania y Polonia. También se prevé la asistencia de responsables de la Unión Europea y de la OTAN. El portavoz del Kremlin, Dmitri Peskov, dijo a los periodistas que Witkoff podría informar a Putin sobre la postura de los ucranianos y los europeos cuando se reunieran. No dio más detalles. Algunos medios de comunicación estadounidenses han informado de que Witkoff podría reunirse con Putin el miércoles en San Petersburgo.

item.title: OpenAI busca acelerar captação de recursos antes da abertura de capital da Anthropic, dizem fontes
item.description: A OpenAI está correndo contra o tempo para garantir compromissos de investidores antes da esperada estreia da rival Anthropic no mercado de capitais, prevista para meados de novembro, em uma captação de recursos excepcionalmente rápida que poderia avaliar a fabricante do ChatGPT em mais de US$1,4 trilhão, segundo duas fontes a par do assunto.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A OpenAI está correndo contra o tempo para garantir compromissos de investidores antes da esperada estreia da rival Anthropic no mercado de capitais, prevista para meados de novembro, em uma captação de recursos excepcionalmente rápida que poderia avaliar a fabricante do ChatGPT em mais de US$1,4 trilhão, segundo duas fontes a par do assunto. O cronograma acelerado reflete, em parte, o desejo de ficar à frente da Anthropic, já que as duas empresas estão cada vez mais atraindo uma base semelhante de investidores, disseram as fontes, acrescentando que a OpenAI quer capitalizar sobre seu recente crescimento de receita após o lançamento de novos modelos. O SoftBank Group (9984.T) , a MGX, com sede em Abu Dhabi, e outros investidores atuais da OpenAI estão em negociações para participar da rodada de financiamento de cerca de US$30 bilhões, disse uma das fontes. Essa aceleração ressalta o quão acirrada é a competição entre as duas desenvolvedoras de IA por capital, já que ambas buscam avaliações na casa de trilhões de dólares, em meio a preocupações crescentes com o aumento das taxas de juros, a volatilidade significativa das ações do setor de tecnologia e o crescente escrutínio sobre as avaliações das empresas de IA. A OpenAI realizou reuniões com fundos de investimento de longo prazo e fundos soberanos na semana passada, enquanto a Anthropic realizava seu próprio dia do investidor. Espera-se que a rodada de financiamento da OpenAI avance mais rapidamente do que o habitual para uma oferta desse porte, disseram as fontes. Investidores familiarizados com a empresa afirmam que a OpenAI também precisa de capital para financiar seus substanciais compromissos de infraestrutura e fortalecer seu balanço patrimonial, caso uma deterioração nos mercados de IPO atrase ainda mais sua listagem prevista para 2027. Embora haja alta demanda pelas ações de ambas as empresas, os investidores enfrentam o desafio de avaliar e alocar capital para duas ofertas complexas e concorrentes com poucos dias ou semanas de diferença entre si. Alguns investidores veem a iniciativa de financiamento da OpenAI como um esforço para garantir capital de fundos que, de outra forma, poderiam dedicar mais de seus recursos ao IPO da Anthropic, disseram as fontes. A OpenAI e a SoftBank se recusaram a comentar. A Anthropic e a MGX não responderam imediatamente aos pedidos de comentário. (Reportagem de Echo Wang e Sabrina Valle, em Nova York, e Krystal Hu, em San Francisco)

item.title: BC prepara ações para conter endividamento e analisa modelo que limita crédito sem garantia
item.description: O Banco Central prepara um conjunto de medidas com o objetivo de conter o crescente endividamento das famílias no país, incluindo ações para ampliar responsabilidades e exigir transparência por parte dos bancos, e analisa um modelo regulatório que limita o crédito autorizado por pessoa a depender do nível de renda, disseram à Reuters duas fontes que participam das discussões.
item.dc:creator: Bernardo Caram, Marcela Ayres
item.content:encoded: O Banco Central prepara um conjunto de medidas com o objetivo de conter o crescente endividamento das famílias no país, incluindo ações para ampliar responsabilidades e exigir transparência por parte dos bancos, e analisa um modelo regulatório que limita o crédito autorizado por pessoa a depender do nível de renda, disseram à Reuters duas fontes que participam das discussões. O plano reflete a crescente preocupação de autoridades com o comprometimento das finanças das famílias. O BC já havia sinalizado que anunciaria [USN:S0N43T00G TEXT:"medidas"] para disciplinar a oferta de crédito sem garantia, incluindo via cartões de crédito. De acordo com as duas fontes familiarizadas com os debates, que falaram sob anonimato devido à natureza privada das ações, as medidas devem ser faseadas e anunciadas de maneira gradual, sendo que eventual aumento de requerimento de capital para as instituições financeiras não deverá constar em uma primeira leva de anúncios. O Banco Central afirmou que não comentaria o assunto. O endividamento é tema central nas discussões eleitorais no país, com o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que tenta a reeleição, tendo colocado em prática novas rodadas de renegociação e perdão de dívidas de famílias e empreendedores, enquanto o candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) prometeu implementar um programa de compra de débitos pelo governo e congelamento temporário de dívidas se for vitorioso nas urnas. O endividamento das famílias atingiu em julho 49,9% da renda acumulada nos últimos 12 meses, patamar historicamente alto, segundo dados do BC, e o Serasa apontou um nível recorde de 83,9 milhões de consumidores inadimplentes. Enquanto a expansão dos canais bancários digitais ampliou o acesso ao crédito e reduziu custos para credores e consumidores no país nos últimos anos, a rapidez e a agressividade com que empréstimos podem ser ofertados, aprovados e desembolsados têm levantado questionamentos sobre a concessão responsável desses financiamentos. Um dos eixos em estudo prevê que as instituições financeiras façam uma classificação criteriosa do perfil do tomador antes de conceder o crédito. Também seriam ampliadas exigências de transparência para que o consumidor tenha acesso simplificado às informações da operação antes da contratação, disse uma das fontes. Como parte da revisão de experiências internacionais, a autarquia tem debatido o modelo adotado, entre outros países, por Cingapura, tratado como um exemplo bem-sucedido, ressaltou essa fonte. O sistema do país do sudeste asiático limita o volume de crédito sem garantia, incluindo cartão de crédito, a dois meses de salário do tomador com renda anual de até 30.000 dólares de Cingapura (cerca de US$23.400, ou R$119,2 mil). O teto sobe para quatro meses de salário para quem tem renda entre 30.000 e 120.000 dólares de Cingapura, não havendo limitação para pessoas com rendimento acima desse patamar. Também há no país critérios que demandam comprovação de renda ou patrimônio para que o cliente tenha acesso a um cartão de crédito. A segunda fonte afirmou que as medidas em estudo levam em conta que instituições financeiras devem se orientar por dois conceitos amplamente utilizados em mercados mais desenvolvidos: "affordability" (capacidade de pagamento) e "suitability" (adequação). Na prática, isso significa avaliar não apenas se o tomador de crédito tem capacidade financeira para arcar com as parcelas sem comprometer excessivamente sua renda, mas também se o crédito oferecido é adequado ao seu perfil e necessidade.

item.title: Britain seeks to break Apple's grip on contactless payments
item.description: Britain's competition regulator said on Tuesday it was seeking to loosen Apple's grip on contactless payments by proposing that the company lower fees and remove technical barriers, helping rival services compete with Apple Pay.
item.dc:creator: Paul Sandle
item.content:encoded: Britain's competition regulator said on Tuesday it was seeking to loosen Apple's grip on contactless payments by proposing that the company lower fees and remove technical barriers, helping rival services compete with Apple Pay. The Competition and Markets Authority said its proposals would result in "substantially lower access fees" and easier access to Apple's contactless technology, opening the market to competition from digital banks and other providers. The proposed measures are less onerous than those imposed by the European Union in 2024, which included giving third-party wallet developers free access. Since then, companies including Vipps, PayPal, Klarna, Curve and BBVA have launched alternative payment apps, the CMA said. CMA Chief Executive Sarah Cardell said the proposals would open the door to more innovation and more choice, as well as boosting Britain's important fintech sector. "We have heard that high fees, strict terms, and technical restrictions relating to Apple's contactless technology make it too difficult for challengers to innovate and compete," she said. "By removing barriers to entry, we can help create the conditions for brilliant British businesses with great ideas to develop new products and services here - from payment apps and digital IDs to travel passes and digital keys." The CMA is consulting on the proposals until November 17, before making a final decision. Contactless payments have grown rapidly in popularity, accounting for 39% of all payments, compared with just 3% a decade ago, the CMA said. More than 60% of adults use a digital wallet, with Apple Wallet the most popular in Britain, it added. Apple said it had already made it possible for developers to offer contactless payments in their apps through NFC, which allows an iPhone to talk to a payments terminal or reader, and through its secure element, which stores sensitive material such as card credentials and cryptographic keys. The company said this allowed developers to create products and services, including in-store payments, transit passes and event tickets, while ensuring users' sensitive data remained protected by the highest security standards. "We do not believe the CMA should require Apple to adopt an approach with lower privacy and security protections," an Apple spokesperson said. "We will continue to engage constructively to reach an outcome that is in the best interest of our users."

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Der ukrainische Präsident Wolodymyr Selenskyj reist am Dienstag zu einem Krisentreffen mit dem US-Sondergesandten Steve Witkoff nach Oslo. Ziel ist es, die Beziehungen zu Washington zu kitten, die sich in den vergangenen zwei Wochen drastisch verschlechtert haben, während sich US-Präsident Donald Trump zunehmend Moskau annähert. Trump, der US-Sanktionen gegen Russland ausgesetzt hat, um nach eigenen Angaben die Treibstoffpreise in den USA zu senken, hatte Selenskyj wiederholt kritisiert. Am Montag hatte der US-Präsident erklärt: "Russland hat sich, ehrlich gesagt, in Bezug auf die Ukraine korrekt verhalten." Selenskyj helfe "der Sache nicht gerade". Die Ukraine müsse "jemand anderen für die Verhandlungen" finden. Kiew wirft Washington vor, zuletzt keine Frühwarndaten zu russischen Raketenstarts mehr übermittelt und die für die Steuerung ukrainischer Drohnen wichtigen Satellitenverbindungen des US-Unternehmens SpaceX gedrosselt zu haben. Selenskyj teilte mit, er habe mit US-Außenminister Marco Rubio unter anderem über Abwehrraketen gegen ballistische Raketen, Frühwarnsysteme und die Lage bei den Satellitendiensten Starlink und Starshield gesprochen. Diese müssten wiederhergestellt werden. "Natürlich geschieht dies alles vor dem Hintergrund unserer diplomatischen Initiativen, diesen schrecklichen Krieg und das tägliche Sterben zu beenden", schrieb Selenskyj auf dem Kurznachrichtendienst X. "IN KONSTRUKTIVERE BAHNEN LENKEN" Westeuropäische Staaten betrachten die Verteidigung der Ukraine gegen die russische Invasion als existenziell für die Sicherheit des Kontinents. Sie unterstützen Selenskyj nachdrücklich und versuchen, einen tieferen Bruch zwischen Washington und Kiew abzuwenden. Die USA haben unter Trump die direkte Lieferung von Waffen an die Ukraine weitgehend eingestellt, erlauben europäischen Staaten jedoch, US-Gerät für Kiew zu kaufen. Zudem stellen die USA weiterhin Geheimdienstinformationen und Technologien bereit, die Europa nicht ersetzen kann. Das Ziel des Treffens am Dienstag sei es, "die diplomatischen Bemühungen in konstruktivere Bahnen zu lenken", erklärte der norwegische Ministerpräsident Jonas Gahr Store. An den Gesprächen nimmt neben Witkoff auch Trumps Schwiegersohn Jared Kushner virtuell teil. Beide leiten die Verhandlungen auf US-Seite. Der finnische Präsident Alexander Stubb erklärte, er werde an dem Treffen teilnehmen, um über den "illegalen Angriffskrieg Russlands gegen die Ukraine und die allgemeine Sicherheitslage in Europa" zu beraten. Für den späteren Dienstagnachmittag ist eine gemeinsame Pressekonferenz geplant.

item.title: Otter.ai raises $320 million in non-equity financing to expand enterprise business
item.description: AI meeting-transcription company Otter.ai said on Tuesday it had closed $320 million in growth financing from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund to expand its enterprise business and international reach.
item.dc:creator: Akash Sriram
item.content:encoded: AI meeting-transcription company Otter.ai said on Tuesday it had closed $320 million in growth financing from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund to expand its enterprise business and international reach. The financing is repayable rather than equity, avoiding shareholder dilution, CEO Sam Liang told Reuters. Otter, which began as a consumer app and now has more than 40 million users, aims to at least double its enterprise revenue next year. "We do need to pay them back," Liang said, adding that Otter would repay the fund with interest as sales and marketing spending generates revenue. He said the fund could provide more capital once the initial amount is spent. Liang said Otter plans to double or triple its sales and marketing budget, grow its small sales team and market more heavily abroad. The US is its biggest market, followed by Canada, Britain and India. The company now supports languages including Spanish, French, German, Japanese and Mandarin. The CEO declined to disclose enterprise revenue, the share of users who pay, or the company's target. He said enterprise is Otter's fastest-growing segment and that he hopes to triple its revenue next year. Liang said enterprise customers are more likely to stick with the product because teams use it collectively. About 86% of Fortune 500 companies already have Otter users, mostly through organic adoption, and the company aims to convert them into paying customers, he added. Otter said it has generated more than $1.5 billion in customer return on investment. The estimate draws on user surveys, which found paying customers regain at least four hours a week. It also draws on an analysis by a large asset manager, which found a return of at least $10 per $1 spent. Otter plans an eventual initial public offering, Liang said, but wants to build more enterprise revenue first.

item.title: One in three Americans back second execution attempt after failed one, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
item.description: One-third of Americans think the government should try a second time to put a convicted criminal to death if a first execution attempt fails, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted after a botched lethal injection in Tennessee.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Allen, Jason Lange
item.content:encoded: One-third of Americans think the government should try a second time to put a convicted criminal to death if a first execution attempt fails, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted after a botched [USN:L1N45T0QI TEXT:"lethal injection"] in Tennessee. The four-day poll, completed on Monday, showed 39% of respondents thought the government should instead allow convicts to serve life in prison following a failed execution, while 26% were not sure which was a better approach. The nationwide survey found minority public support for trying again to execute inmates who survive execution attempts, a question Tennessee now faces after [USN:L1N45W052 TEXT:"Christa Pike"], 50, survived two lethal injection attempts last month in Nashville. The convicted murderer was taken to a hospital unconscious following the attempted execution, critically ill and with severe arm injuries after two syringes of the caustic barbiturate pentobarbital failed to kill her, marking Tennessee's second botched lethal injection this year. She did not regain consciousness until five days later. Most countries around the world, along with 23 US states, have abolished capital punishment. Those US states that still impose it have struggled in recent years to obtain execution drugs, and some have considered other methods, including firing squads. A slight majority of Americans — 55% — continue to support capital punishment for people convicted of the most serious crimes, down from 63% who said in a 2017 Reuters/Ipsos poll that they supported the policy. Some 31% of respondents in the latest poll said they opposed the death penalty, while 13% either did not know or did not answer the question. The issue has taken on new significance as courts consider whether states can make a second execution attempt after a failed one. The US Supreme Court [USN:L6N3W5005 TEXT:"recently allowed"] a state to proceed with scheduling a second execution date after a failed attempt. Kenneth Smith, convicted of a 1988 murder-for-hire, survived a trip to Alabama's execution chamber in 2022 after prison officials failed to set up intravenous lines. But Alabama succeeded on its second try in 2024 with a new method of suffocation using nitrogen gas. OPPOSITION TO LIVESTREAMING EXECUTIONS US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth recently floated the prospect of the [USN:L1N46113P TEXT:"first-ever livestream of a US execution"], the planned death by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, the former US Army major who killed 13 people at Texas' Fort Hood military base. Following widespread criticism – including from Republican lawmakers – President Donald Trump canceled the livestream plans, though officials still intend to carry out the execution on December 3. Some 46% of Americans, including 29% of Democrats and 71% of Republicans, said it was appropriate to execute Hasan by firing squad. But 71% of people surveyed, including majorities of Democrats and Republicans, said showing executions to the public on television or the internet was inappropriate. The Reuters/Ipsos poll was conducted online and nationwide, gathering responses from 1,679 US adults. It had a margin of error of 2 percentage points.

item.title: Early US flu season, current strain may signal risk for younger people; doctors urge shots
item.description: Doctors are urging Americans aged 6 months and older to get vaccinated against the flu after an unusual early rise in cases on the West Coast that virologists are still working to understand.
item.dc:creator: Michael Erman, Julie Steenhuysen
item.content:encoded: Doctors are urging Americans aged 6 months and older to get vaccinated against the flu after an unusual early rise in cases on the West Coast that virologists are still working to understand. It could be the strain itself. The predominant flu strain this year is H1N1, which caused the 2009 swine flu pandemic and is now a standard part of the flu shot. But this year’s version of the virus has a new mutation called G155E. People who have been previously exposed to H1N1, either through infection or vaccination, would only have some residual protection from the older versions, scientists say. "What people are a bit worried about is that the H1N1 strain this year hasn't been seen by a lot of younger folk, so it may be more severe in them," said Dr. Jennifer Duchon, a pediatric infectious disease expert at Mount Sinai Children's Hospital in New York, adding that her hospital has started to see some flu cases. The 2026-2027 flu vaccines, approved by the FDA in August, target H1N1, H3N2 — the dominant strain last flu season — and one influenza B virus. While most children recover, flu can be deadly, especially for the very youngest and those with underlying health conditions. Promotion of flu shots has been reduced under US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., a longtime anti-vaccine activist who has engineered an [USN:L8N3Y61FI TEXT:"overhaul of long-standing childhood vaccine schedules"]. The American Medical Association recommends the shot for all people 6 months and older. The vaccine's effectiveness fluctuates depending on how well it is matched months in advance to circulating flu strains. Over the past 10 years, it has been between 30% and 60% effective in reducing flu hospitalizations and deaths. Last year, an estimated 32 million Americans had the flu, 390,000 were hospitalized and 24,000 died. Scott Hensley, a microbiologist at the University of Pennsylvania, said two of the three components of this year's vaccine appear to be very well matched to circulating flu strains. However, the H1N1 mutation might affect antibodies in younger people, and with flu season picking up steam, "it is probably a good idea to get vaccinated early," Hensley said via email. GEOGRAPHY CHANGES Typically, flu cases start in Southern states and move north. This year, it's coming from the west, said Caitlin Rivers, a Johns Hopkins epidemiologist who tracks pathogens in a weekly newsletter called Force of Infection. “There's no clear reason to me why this would be the case,” Rivers said. As last year was dominated by the H3N2, there could be an "immunological gap" because immunity to H1N1 virus is not as fresh. Or, it could be the new mutation, she said. Jeanne Marrazzo, chief executive of the Infectious Diseases Society of America, said studies of antibodies from people exposed to the flu last year found they did not recognize this new mutation. That was especially true of antibodies from teens and young adults. Marrazzo said the small studies were something to be aware of but not cause for alarm. FALLING SHOTS, RISING FLU CASES Some 58 million American adults received a flu shot last season, according to data firm IQVIA, down more than 20% from the nearly 75 million in the 2019-20 season, the last season before the COVID-19 pandemic changed US vaccination patterns. Around half of US children got flu shots last year, according to CDC data, compared with more than 60% in 2019-20. Standard flu shots are made by GSK (GSK.L) , Sanofi (SASY.PA) , and CSL's (CSL.AX) Seqirus unit. AstraZeneca (AZN.L) makes a nasal spray inoculation called FluMist. A new mRNA vaccine from Moderna (MRNA.O) is also available. Vaccine manufacturers say demand has been consistent with last year. Two pharmacists told Reuters vaccination rates have not picked up significantly. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention dropped its recommendation for the shot for most children at the beginning of 2025, a move a court put on hold. CDC also pulled its ad campaign to promote flu vaccination in 2025, according to press reports. Paul Offit, a pediatric infectious disease expert at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, said he believes immunization rates have been hurt by HHS' decision to cut back on promoting flu shots, as well as by statements from Kennedy himself. "He has done what he can to discourage flu vaccination," Offit said. When asked about public health messaging on flu shots this season, HHS spokesperson Emily Hilliard pointed to the CDC's "Respiratory Illness Season Toolkit" on the agency's website. It says vaccination is the most effective tool to prevent serious illness. Flu activity is low but has been on the rise since late August, CDC data show. Positive tests reported to the CDC by clinical labs last week hit a 10-year high for this time of year at 5%. On the West Coast, that figure was 10.7%, compared with 0.5% a year earlier. At peak flu, the rates are around 30%. Numbers are also elevated in eight Southern states including Florida and South Carolina, according to Hopkins' Rivers.

item.title: Mapping the Market: Canadian dollar could make a comeback against US dollar
item.description: The Canadian dollar has lost ground to the US currency for more than a month, but that may be starting to change, technical analysis suggests.
item.dc:creator: Paul Spirgel, Robert Fullem
item.content:encoded: The Canadian dollar has lost ground to the US currency for more than a month, but that may be starting to change, technical analysis suggests. Click here for a detailed technical analysis chart. Technical analysis uses charts of past price moves to help predict where a market might go next. Analysts look especially for support and resistance. Support is a price level that acts like a floor when a market is falling. Resistance acts like a ceiling when a market is rising. Traders often find these levels using previous highs and lows, or moving averages. A moving average is the average price over a set number of days, drawn as a smooth line that shows the underlying trend. The Canadian dollar is usually quoted as Canadian dollars per US dollar, so a falling line means the Canadian dollar, also called the loonie, is getting stronger. From late August to early October, the US dollar gained about 4% against the loonie. It reached a 1-1/2-year high of 1.43 Canadian dollars, according to data supplied by LSEG. The climb was driven by rising US bond yields and expectations that the Federal Reserve would be aggressive in raising interest rates. Higher rates make a currency more attractive to investors. That began to change over the last week or so. US bond yields retreated, and investors reconsidered how much tightening they expect from the Fed. This has given the loonie an opening, and it has pulled the US dollar lower, wiping out more than a third of the earlier rally. Markets rarely move in a straight line, and pullbacks of this size are common. The next step is to see whether the loonie can keep its momentum. If it pushes the US dollar below 1.4039, where the 100-day moving average sits, that could open the way to further gains. Traders would then target the 200-day moving average at 1.3880. Analysts watch that line closely because it reflects the long-term trend. Below that is 1.3734, the August low and the starting point of the US dollar's most recent rally against the loonie. On the other hand, there is also a risk that the pullback fades. If the US dollar rebounds above the 21-day moving average at 1.4185 and the 10-day moving average at 1.4208, the loonie's recovery prospects would dissipate. Those shorter-term averages show where prices have been trading recently. The US dollar could then make another attempt to break through resistance in the 1.43 to 1.44 zone. item.title: Could disillusioned Kansas voters send their first Democrat to the US Senate in 94 years?
item.description: The last time the state of Kansas sent a Democrat to the US Senate, the Great Depression was ravaging the state, wheat prices had collapsed and drought was turning the Great Plains into the Dust Bowl.
item.dc:creator: Renee Hickman
item.content:encoded: The last time the state of Kansas sent a Democrat to the US Senate, the Great Depression was ravaging the state, wheat prices had collapsed and drought was turning the Great Plains into the Dust Bowl. Some 94 years later, Kansas may do it again. Opinion polls show Democratic candidate Adam Hamilton, a megachurch pastor, running neck and neck with or ahead of Republican US Senator Roger Marshall in a state that Republican President Donald Trump won in 2024 with more than 57% of the vote. The unexpectedly competitive race reflects strains in the Republican heartland, where Democrats are betting that soaring farm costs, including near-record-high diesel, and discontent with Trump's immigration crackdown can revive the region's progressive populist tradition. In the converted grain bin that serves as an office for Vance and Louise Ehmke's wheat farm and seed business, John Brown, the abolitionist who took up arms against slavery in Kansas, stares down from a reproduction of a famous painting. In 1885, 20 years after the Civil War, Vance Ehmke’s ancestors started farming in western Kansas. But now, climbing costs linked to the US-Israeli war on Iran have him contemplating a dark future for his farm and others around it. “During the past year, we have seen fuel prices just darn near double,” Ehmke said. “That’s cost us $50,000 of unexpected expenses.” COST OF FUEL, FERTILIZER Fuel and fertilizer prices have [USN:L6N45S116 TEXT:"shot up"] dramatically since the war started in February, with [USN:L1N45U0FQ TEXT:"diesel"] used to power farm equipment up 70% since the war began. Those rising costs have reverberated in states like Kansas, Iowa and Nebraska, where agriculture dominates local economies. In Iowa, opinion polls show Republican US Representative Ashley Hinson in a tight Senate race with Democrat Josh Turek for the seat [USN:L6N45U0XV TEXT:"being vacated"] by Republican Joni Ernst. Hinson called last month for an "immediate end" to the Iran war in a social media post that said Iowans "shouldn't have to foot the bill at the pump or the checkout line for the war." In Nebraska, Republican Senator Pete Ricketts faces a competitive race against independent Dan Osborn, despite Trump winning the state by more than 20 points in 2024. Democrats need to pick up four US Senate seats to win control of the chamber. TRUMP, JD VANCE STUMP FOR AT-RISK REPUBLICANS Trump, Vice President JD Vance and other Republicans have stumped for at-risk candidates in the Midwest region. Trump pledged in Nebraska this month to expand access to tax-exempt diesel fuel and planned a rally this week in the Wichita area. Hamilton still has an uphill climb with many rural Kansas voters. Not far from the Ehmkes is another farm owned by Ron Suppes, a Republican who supports Marshall. “We’ve had high diesel prices in prior years. I don’t know if it matters which administration,” he said. “I’ll put up with the pain for a while." Another Trump priority hit the Kansas meatpacking industry in late September, when Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents arrested 104 people in Dodge City, Garden City, Liberal and surrounding areas, according to the US Attorney's Office for the District of Kansas. Amid voter anger over high beef prices, the raids [USN:L1N45G16V TEXT:"slowed operations"] at major processors including Cargill and National Beef as some employees stayed home for fear of arrest. The raids may also have affected the traditionally conservative politics of those towns. Wichita State University's IKE Lab found a significant jump in September voter registrations in counties where the ICE raids took place, researcher and professor Alexandra Middlewood said. VOTER REGISTRATIONS RISE Oscar Soto, a grocery store owner in Dodge City, was shocked when he began seeing social media reports of ICE agents flooding his town on September 22. He joined with a group of community organizers to take meals to families afraid to leave home or whose providers had been arrested. He said what he saw that week as he volunteered inspired him to register to vote for the first time at the age of 39. “What can I do to help make any difference at all?" he said he asked himself. "And the one thing I landed on was voting." He said he planned to vote for the Democrat. In the 2024 election, Trump won nearly half the Hispanic vote, but an October 5 Reuters/Ipsos poll showed [USN:L6N45R10Y TEXT:"just 24%"] of Hispanic Americans now approve of Trump's performance in the White House. Hispanic voters made up more than 9% of Kansas voters in 2024, according to the Pew Research Center. CAMPAIGNS TRADE ATTACKS Marshall's campaign has criticized Hamilton over an incident in which a volunteer at a camp connected to his church was accused of molesting two teenage boys. Church leaders initially only investigated the incident internally, later reporting it to police when the volunteer returned to the camp and was again accused of inappropriate behavior. Hamilton has since said the church should have gone to police first and that it changed its policy after the incident to require that. Hamilton’s campaign, in turn, has highlighted a September New York Times report that Marshall, an obstetrician before entering politics, sued more than 700 patients over unpaid medical bills. Marshall said he had followed typical collection practices. Marshall’s campaign did not respond to a request for an interview but issued a statement that said in part he had delivered for farmers, cut middle-class taxes and secured the border, and sought to tie Hamilton to national Democrats, calling him a “Chuck Schumer-funded Democrat,” referring to the Senate minority leader from New York. In Garden City on October 9, a group of voters awaited Hamilton’s visit in a small café, including Michael Shull, a retired pediatrician and registered Republican. Shull said he supported Hamilton because of his moderate political stances and because “he’s willing to talk to people.” Speaking to Reuters after the event, Hamilton zeroed in on the message sent by voters like Shull in reliably Republican Kansas. “It’s not just that Kansas is in play, and we might flip a seat,” Hamilton said. “It’s that people in a reliably red state are saying what’s happening in Washington, DC, is not OK.”

item.title: Brazil central bank looks to encourage responsible lending in consumer debt crackdown, sources say
item.description: Brazil's central bank is preparing a package of measures to curb rising household indebtedness, including stricter disclosure requirements for lenders, while studying foreign regulatory models that limit access to unsecured credit based on borrowers' income, two people involved in the discussions told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Marcela Ayres, Bernardo Caram
item.content:encoded: Brazil's central bank is preparing a package of measures to curb rising household indebtedness, including stricter disclosure requirements for lenders, while studying foreign regulatory models that limit access to unsecured credit based on borrowers' income, two people involved in the discussions told Reuters. The move reflects growing concern among policymakers over household debt levels and the rapid expansion of unsecured lending. The central bank has already signaled it plans to unveil measures to tighten oversight of unsecured credit, including credit card lending. According to the people familiar with the discussions, who spoke on condition of anonymity due to the private nature of deliberations, the measures are expected to be rolled out gradually, with any increase in capital requirements unlikely to feature in an initial package. The central bank declined to comment. The review comes as household finances have become a central issue in Brazil's presidential campaign, with President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva rolling out measures aimed at boosting consumers' purchasing power amid record consumer indebtedness in Latin America's largest economy. Lula unexpectedly finished behind right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in the first round of voting, setting up a runoff on Sunday. Recent polls show Bolsonaro is narrowly favored to win. While digital channels have broadened access to credit and lowered borrowing costs in Brazil, they have also made it easier for loans to be marketed, approved and disbursed faster than ever, raising questions about responsible lending practices. One proposal under consideration would require lenders to conduct more rigorous assessments of borrowers' financial circumstances before extending credit. Authorities are also considering stronger disclosure rules to give consumers clearer and more accessible information about loan terms before signing contracts, said one source. As part of its review of international experience, the central bank has examined frameworks adopted in several jurisdictions, including Singapore, which one of the sources described as a successful example. Singapore limits unsecured borrowing, including credit card debt, for lower-income consumers. Individuals earning up to around 30,000 Singapore dollars ($23,435) a year can generally hold unsecured debt equivalent to up to two months of income, while the cap rises to four months of income for those earning between 30,000 and 120,000 Singapore dollars. No such limit applies to higher-income earners. The country also imposes income and asset-related requirements for access to certain credit products. A second source said the discussions had been guided by two concepts widely used in more developed credit markets: affordability and suitability. In practice, that means assessing not only whether borrowers can reasonably service a loan without undue strain on their finances, but also whether the credit product being offered is appropriate for their circumstances and needs. ($1 = 1.2801 Singapore dollars)

item.title: German regulator fines Nomura over Commerzbank disclosure breaches
item.description: German financial regulator Bafin said on Tuesday it had fined Japanese investment firm Nomura Holdings €320,000 ($359,000) for failing to disclose voting rights in Commerzbank as UniCredit built its stake in the German lender.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: German financial regulator Bafin said on Tuesday it had fined Japanese investment firm Nomura Holdings (8604.T) €320,000 ($359,000) for failing to disclose voting rights in Commerzbank (CBKG.DE) as UniCredit (CRDI.MI) built its stake in the German lender. The regulator said Nomura did not submit voting rights notifications relating to Commerzbank in May and June Under German law, shareholders must notify the issuer and the regulator within four trading days if their voting rights reach certain thresholds If a shareholder does not comply, Bafin can impose a fine of up to €10 million or 5% of total revenue "Whilst we do not comment on the details of our interactions with regulators, the firm takes adherence to regulations seriously," a Nomura spokesperson told Reuters The company can appeal the administrative fine order, Bafin said ($1 = 0.8916 euros)

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El gigante energético italiano Enel (ENEI.MI) dijo el martes que no tiene intención de reducir su participación en la empresa eléctrica española Endesa (ELE.MC) . "Enel niega categóricamente, como ya ha hecho en varias ocasiones en el pasado, cualquier intención de reducir, ni siquiera parcialmente, su participación en Endesa", dijo un portavoz de Enel en un comunicado tras la publicación de una noticia en un medio español. item.title: Colombian Congress approves $201.1 billion budget for 2027
item.description: Colombian lawmakers approved spending distributions for next year's 634.9 trillion pesos ($201.14 billion) budget early on Tuesday, trimming spending linked to a 10-year-old peace agreement, boosting defense funds and reducing debt service payments.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Colombian lawmakers approved spending distributions for next year's 634.9 trillion pesos ($201.14 billion) budget early on Tuesday, trimming spending linked to a 10-year-old peace agreement, boosting defense funds and reducing debt service payments. The budget, which projects a 2027 fiscal deficit of 9.4% of gross domestic product, is a significant increase from the 555.8 trillion peso budget for this year. The 2027 budget allocates 144 trillion pesos ($45.62 billion) for debt repayment, 93 trillion pesos for education, 81.6 trillion pesos for health, and 74.9 trillion pesos for defense. The bigger budget comes as Colombia, Latin America's fourth-largest economy, struggles to put its public accounts in order. Public debt is expected to rise this year and next, moving the country further from regaining the investment-grade rating it lost in 2021. The government of new right-wing President Abelardo De La Espriella had promised to trim remaining spending for this year and said it plans to propose a "Rescue Law" to Congress to cut 2027 spending and reduce the fiscal deficit to 7.2% of GDP. Lawmakers in the lower house approved the budget bill with 112 votes in favor and only one against it. "Thank you all for giving us this vote of confidence. We are going to succeed in getting the country out of this very complex economic situation," Finance Minister Miguel Gomez said after the Senate passed the bill on Monday. SPENDING CUTS The budget cuts funds for the Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP) - the court created under a 2016 peace deal with the former Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) guerrillas to try rebel leaders and ex-soldiers for war crimes. It also reduces operational funding for the Search Unit for Disappeared People (UBPD), created under the peace deal to look for at least 137,000 people who vanished during the ongoing armed conflict. The two entities and advocates say the cuts will [USN:L6N45R12F TEXT:"limit investigations and trials"] into human rights violations, as well as exhumations and identifications of the disappeared. ($1 = 3,156.5000 Colombian pesos)

item.title: Ações da China e de Hong Kong caem; crescimento estável diminui expectativas de estímulos

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: As ações das principais empresas da China e as de Hong Kong registraram queda nesta terça-feira, acompanhando uma retração mais ampla na região, depois que Pequim manteve inalteradas as principais taxas de juros e dados mais sólidos do PIB atenuaram as expectativas de novos estímulos. No fechamento, o índice de Xangai (.SSEC) teve alta de 0,1%, enquanto o índice CSI300 (.CSI300) , que reúne as maiores companhias listadas em Xangai e Shenzhen, recuou 0,5%. O Índice CSI de Bancos (.CSI399986) caiu 0,9%, enquanto o setor financeiro (.CSI300FS) registrou perda de 1,2%. O setor relacionado ao ouro (.CSI931238) recuou 1,8%, à medida que os preços do ouro continuaram a cair. O índice composto ChiNext, voltado para startups (.CNT) , recuou 0,3%, e o índice STAR50 de Xangai, com foco em tecnologia (.STAR50) , subiu 1%. Em Hong Kong, o índice de referência Hang Seng (.HSI) registrou queda de 1,3%, e o índice Hang Seng Tech (.HSTECH) recuou 1,5%, atingindo a menor cotação em dois anos. Em um sinal de que as autoridades não têm pressa em implementar novas medidas de flexibilização monetária após os sólidos dados do PIB, a China manteve suas taxas de juros de referência inalteradas pela 17ª vez consecutiva na terça-feira, em linha com as expectativas do mercado. A economia chinesa se recuperou de uma mínima de três anos no último trimestre, crescendo 4,5% e superando as estimativas, à medida que as exportações robustas compensaram a demanda interna fraca. As ações asiáticas recuaram de maneira generalizada na terça-feira, enquanto o petróleo subia, já que os riscos geopolíticos abalaram o ânimo dos investidores antes da divulgação de resultados importantes de empresas líderes no setor de IA. . Em TÓQUIO, o índice Nikkei (.N225) caiu 1,3%, a 64.075 pontos. . Em HONG KONG, o índice HANG SENG (.HSI) caiu 1,32%, a 23.867 pontos. . Em XANGAI, o índice SSEC (.SSEC) ganhou 0,12%, a 3.735 pontos. . O índice CSI300 (.CSI300) , que reúne as maiores companhias listadas em XANGAI e SHENZHEN, retrocedeu 0,54%, a 4.152 pontos. . item.title: Azul prevê recuperação mais demorada devido à pressão dos custos com combustível
item.description: A companhia aérea brasileira Azul prevê que sua recuperação demore mais do que se esperava inicialmente e mantém um plano de crescimento cauteloso, disse o diretor financeiro Antonio Carlos Garcia à Reuters, já que os altos preços do combustível de aviação continuam pressionando as margens, mesmo depois que a empresa saiu da recuperação judicial prevista no Chapter 11 no início deste ano.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A companhia aérea brasileira Azul (AZUL3.SA) prevê que sua recuperação demore mais do que se esperava inicialmente e mantém um plano de crescimento cauteloso, disse o diretor financeiro Antonio Carlos Garcia à Reuters, já que os altos preços do combustível de aviação continuam pressionando as margens, mesmo depois que a empresa saiu da recuperação judicial prevista no Chapter 11 no início deste ano. A Azul ainda espera encerrar 2026 com uma capacidade cerca de 5% menor em relação ao ano anterior, refletindo uma estratégia que a companhia já havia adotado antes do mais recente impacto nos preços do combustível, disse Garcia na noite de segunda-feira, à margem de uma conferência organizada pela Associação de Transporte Aéreo da América Latina e do Caribe. “Vemos uma recuperação em um estágio mais tardio do que antes”, disse Garcia, acrescentando que o cronograma pode se atrasar em um ano ou mais se os preços do combustível permanecerem elevados. A Azul reduziu a capacidade no segundo trimestre em mais de 10% em relação ao ano anterior, em resposta à alta nos preços dos combustíveis, com a expectativa de que um crescimento modesto da capacidade seja retomado a partir do quarto trimestre. Garcia disse que a Azul já está restabelecendo algumas frequências e colocando de volta em serviço aeronaves que estavam fora de operação, mas ressaltou que isso não deve ser visto como uma expansão agressiva. A companhia aérea conseguiu repassar de 60% a 65% dos aumentos no preço do combustível de aviação aos clientes por meio das tarifas, acrescentou ele. A Azul saiu do Chapter 11 em fevereiro, após reestruturar seu balanço patrimonial, e informou em agosto que a dívida total havia caído para R$21,4 bilhões. Garcia disse que a Azul está se aproximando de um fluxo de caixa livre positivo operacionalmente, mas que a geração de caixa ainda está sendo prejudicada por pagamentos vinculados à reestruturação, tanto anteriores quanto posteriores ao processo do Chapter 11. A Azul também está se apoiando cada vez mais em setores de seu negócio além do transporte de passageiros, incluindo seu programa de fidelidade, serviços de viagem, operações de carga e manutenção, disse Garcia. Questionado sobre os rumores de uma maior consolidação na aviação latino-americana, Garcia disse que a Azul estava focada em “reestruturar” seus próprios negócios, em vez de avaliar possíveis acordos. No ano passado, a controladora da concorrente Gol, a , abandonou as negociações de fusão para unir as duas companhias aéreas, embora tenha deixado a porta aberta para retomar as discussões no futuro. (Reportagem de Kylie Madry)

item.title: Zelenskiy to meet Witkoff as Trump praises Russia and rebukes Ukraine
item.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskiy was due in Oslo to meet US special envoy Steve Witkoff, trying to repair ties with Washington that have deteriorated this month as President Donald Trump has courted Moscow.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskiy was due on Tuesday in Oslo to meet US special envoy Steve Witkoff, trying to repair ties with Washington that have deteriorated this month as President Donald Trump has courted Moscow. Trump, who has waived sanctions on Russia in what he says is an effort to lower US fuel prices, has repeatedly rebuked Zelenskiy and called for him to be [USN:L6N45W06G TEXT:"replaced"]. Kyiv says that Washington has lately failed to provide early warning of Russian missile launches, throttled SpaceX's Starshield satellite links that guide Ukrainian drones, and failed to deliver air defences paid for by European allies. In the latest comments expressing warmth towards Moscow and coldness towards Kyiv, Trump said on Monday: "Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine." Zelenskiy was "not helping matters much" and Kyiv should find "somebody else to negotiate" an end to Russia's war in Ukraine. As relations between Kyiv and Washington have deteriorated, Russia has stepped up its attacks on Ukrainian cities. Both sides have attacked each other's energy systems and data centres, although Ukraine held back for several days on hitting Russian oil refineries at Trump's behest while Moscow showed no sign of limiting strikes. Ukraine says the Russian strikes have become even deadlier because of the absence of US technology needed to fend them off. In the latest attacks, Ukrainian officials said a Russian drone struck near a petrol station on a highway heading south out of the capital, killing three people and setting cars ablaze. Footage released by Ukraine's emergency services showed firefighters battling a huge blaze, surrounded by twisted wreckage in the nighttime darkness. ZELENSKIY SPEAKS TO RUBIO Zelenskiy said he had spoken with Secretary of State Marco Rubio about issues including ballistic missile interceptors, early warning of Russian attacks and "the situation with Starlink/Starshield, which needs to be restored". "Of course, all of this comes against the backdrop of our diplomatic efforts to end this horrific war and the constant killing of people," Zelenskiy said in a post on X. The deterioration of relations began 10 days ago when Trump lifted sanctions on Russian diesel to help lower prices. High fuel costs since he launched strikes on Iran have hurt his Republicans ahead of legislative elections next month. Trump has since repeatedly berated Zelenskiy over Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries, which Kyiv says are one of its few ways of fighting back after nearly five years of intensive Russian bombardment. Trump later issued a broad waiver for tougher sanctions on Russia that were meant to have begun this week under a new bipartisan law named for late Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, a Trump ally and staunch supporter of Ukraine who died in July. Washington denies withholding intelligence from Kyiv or imposing curbs on Starshield, the military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink communications system. Kyiv says the system's receptors no longer work when mounted on fast-moving objects such as its drones. SpaceX boss Elon Musk has said Starshield is controlled by the US government and any limits on its use are ultimately up to Trump. Western European countries consider defending Ukraine from Russia's invasion to be an existential issue for the continent's security and have strongly backed Zelenskiy, seeking to head off a deeper rupture between Washington and Kyiv. The United States under Trump has already largely stopped providing weapons to Ukraine, but allows European countries to buy them on Kyiv's behalf and provides intelligence and technology that Europe can't match. Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere said the goal of hosting Tuesday's meetings was "to steer the diplomatic efforts onto a more constructive path". Finland is co-hosting Tuesday's talks, and its President Alexander Stubb said he would attend meetings with Zelenskiy and Stoere, to discuss "Russia's illegal war of aggression against Ukraine and the overall security situation in Europe." Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner was expected to attend meetings virtually, Norway said. Witkoff and Kushner have led US negotiating efforts. Zelenskiy, Stubb and Stoere will hold a press conference later on Tuesday, Norway said.

item.title: How (and why) we developed ‘The Age of Heat Storms’
item.description: A Reuters reporter got frustrated by a disconnect between climate scientists and the public. So he decided to take a new look at a familiar phenomenon: heat waves. What he found was something much bigger: heat storms.
item.dc:creator: Maurice Tamman
item.content:encoded: I have been writing about climate change and climate scientists for years, and I have been frustrated by a disconnect between scientists and the public that I’ve seen time and again. Scientists and researchers often discuss global warming in the context of risks that will arise if the planet’s average global temperature rises more than 2 degrees Celsius (3.6 degrees Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial levels. Scientists aside, what is an ordinary person to make of that? Not much, in my experience. Another frustration: There is no shortage of stories predicting the dire consequences we face if we don’t find a way to stop the planet’s temperature from rising beyond that threshold. But what about now? What has already happened? And why do these dire warnings so often land with a shrug? Read more at https://www.reuters.com/investigates/special-report/climate-heatstorms-methodology/

item.title: Takeaways: Key findings from our investigation of supersized heat waves
item.description: Reuters conducted a data-driven examination of global temperatures that shows heat waves have surged in size and frequency since the 1960s. These are the key takeaways.
item.dc:creator: Maurice Tamman
item.content:encoded: Heat waves have evolved from sporadic, isolated episodes to massive, cascading weather events that blanket vast swaths of the planet for months or even years at a time. To continue calling such sprawling phenomena “heat waves” would be like calling a monsoon a rain shower. To understand the new reality of these immense expanses of heat, Reuters consulted with two dozen climate researchers and analyzed temperatures around the globe for every hour of every day since 1960. From those results, we developed a new concept: the “heat storm.” Scientists and researchers often discuss global warming in the context of risks that will arise if the planet’s average global temperature rises more than 2°C (3.6°F) above pre-industrial levels. What is an ordinary person to make of that? Not much. Heat waves are the connective tissue between the science of global warming and our everyday experience. But supersized heat waves used to be rare. No longer. Now they swarm the planet. Naming events is “a powerful way for people to understand that something is happening,” Anthony Leiserowitz, director of the Yale Program on Climate Change Communication, told Reuters. Yet “we don't currently do that with heat waves,” he said, even though heat has been estimated to kill almost half a million people a year. item.description: Supersized heat waves used to be rare. No longer. A Reuters data-driven examination of global temperatures reveals what we call ‘heat storms.’ They now swarm the planet, upending life around the world.
item.dc:creator: Maurice Tamman, Ben Welsh, Pete McKenzie, Charlie Szymanski, Delgerzaya Delgerjargal, Robbie Corey-Boulet, Loucoumane Coulibaly, Jeff Horwitz, Joan Faus
item.content:encoded: In less than a lifetime, about six and a half decades, heat waves have evolved from sporadic, isolated episodes to massive, cascading weather events that can blanket vast swaths of the planet for months or even years at a time. The largest heat wave of the 1960s reached about 6% of the planet as it drifted for 46 days over the Atlantic Ocean, parts of Latin America and West Africa. The largest one this decade swept across almost 85% of the globe during its 367-day lifetime, stretching into the polar latitudes and touching virtually every human being on Earth. Read more at https://www.reuters.com/investigates/special-report/climate-heatstorms-science/

item.title: Enel denies report that it seeks to reduce stake in Spain's Endesa
item.description: Italian energy giant Enel said on Tuesday it has no plan to reduce its stake in Spanish power utility Endesa .
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Italian energy giant Enel (ENEI.MI) said on Tuesday it has no plan to reduce its stake in Spanish power utility Endesa (ELE.MC) . "Enel categorically denies, as it has done several times in the past, any intention to reduce, even partially, its stake in Endesa," an Enel spokesperson said in a statement following a report in a Spanish outlet. "Enel is confident that this statement will definitively put an end to such speculations, which have also been published in the past in Spain without any basis," the statement said. "All the plans presented by Enel and the commitments made to the market envisage growth in Europe and the Americas and there can be no other direction than the one approved," it added.

item.title: Pékin accuse la marine US d'incursion "illégale" en mer de Chine méridionale
item.description: L'armée chinoise a annoncé mardi avoir déployé des forces navales après l'incursion "illégale" d'un navire de guerre américain dans des eaux territoriales disputées en mer de Chine méridionale.
item.dc:creator: Liz Lee, Ben Blanchard
item.content:encoded: L'armée chinoise a annoncé mardi avoir déployé des forces navales après l'incursion "illégale" d'un navire de guerre américain dans des eaux territoriales disputées en mer de Chine méridionale. De son côté, Taïwan a fait état d'une escarmouche avec un navire chinois. La Chine revendique la souveraineté de la quasi-totalité de la mer de Chine méridionale malgré les prétentions à la fois du Brunei, de la Malaisie, des Philippines, de Taïwan et du Vietnam sur ces eaux. Le commandement du théâtre sud de l'armée chinoise a déclaré que l'USS Charleston s'était "introduit illégalement" dans des eaux adjacentes au banc Sabina, dans l'archipel des îles Spratleys, sans l'autorisation du gouvernement chinois mardi matin. "Cette action des Etats-Unis porte atteinte aux droits de souveraineté et aux intérêts de la Chine, met en danger la sécurité maritime et nuit à la paix et à la stabilité dans la région", a dénoncé l'armée chinoise dans un communiqué. "La partie américaine doit immédiatement cesser de telles activités." La marine chinoise a ajouté avoir déployé des forces navales pour suivre et surveiller le navire américain. La marine américaine n'a pas répondu dans l'immédiat à une demande de commentaire. Washington qualifie généralement ces missions d'"opérations de liberté de navigation", même si le dernier exercice de ce type effectué en mer de Chine méridionale remonte à plus d'un an. ESCARMOUCHE ENTRE TAÏWAN ET LA CHINE Selon un porte-parole de l'armée philippine, le navire américain "n'a pas pénétré illégalement dans le territoire chinois", ajoutant que Pékin n'avait aucune juridiction pour demander l'autorisation de "transiter légalement dans des eaux internationales". Le mois dernier, un navire des garde-côtes chinois a percuté un bateau philippin en mission près du même banc de sable, selon les garde-côtes philippins. Pékin a imputé à Manille la responsabilité de l'accident. La Chine et les Philippines, ces derniers étant liés par un traité de défense mutuelle avec les Etats-Unis, revendiquent la souveraineté du banc Sabina et de l'archipel des îles Spratleys. Par ailleurs, les garde-côtes taïwanais ont accusé un navire chinois d'avoir pénétré dans des eaux interdites près des îles Pratas, à l'extrémité nord de la mer de Chine méridionale, contrôlées par Taipei. Le navire "Taichung" a été déployé pour lancer un avertissement au bateau chinois, les deux bâtiments diffusant des messages à destination de l'autre, selon les garde-côtes taïwanais. Le Bureau chinois des affaires de Taïwan n'a pas répondu dans l'immédiat à une demande de commentaires. Les îles Pratas se situent en mer de Chine méridionale entre Taipei et Hong Kong et la sécurité de l'archipel relève de la responsabilité du gouvernement taïwanais. La Chine revendique Taïwan, île gouvernée démocratiquement, comme faisant partie de son territoire, bien que Taipei rejette cette revendication de souveraineté.

item.title: Amazon to invest over €16 billion in Germany next year
item.description: Amazon plans to invest more than €16 billion (about $18 billion) in Germany in 2027, the company said on Tuesday, to expand its cloud computing, AI, satellite internet and media businesses.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Amazon (AMZN.O) plans to invest more than €16 billion (about $18 billion) in Germany in 2027, the company said on Tuesday, to expand its cloud computing, AI, satellite internet and media businesses. The investment is the e-commerce giant's latest move to grow its European operations as it races to expand cloud infrastructure across the region amid surging demand for AI services and growing competition among technology firms. The package, announced at the Invest in Germany Summit in Berlin, adds to more than €100 billion Amazon says it has invested in the country since 2010. The latest investment includes €4.8 billion to expand Amazon Web Services' Frankfurt cloud region and AI infrastructure. It also includes new logistics projects expected to create more than 3,000 jobs, development of the Amazon Leo satellite broadband network, and new Prime Video productions. Amazon also plans to open a second robotics and AI research lab in Berlin. Tuesday's commitment follows a [USN:L8N3IH0S8 TEXT:"€10 billion investment"] announced in June 2024 to expand its cloud infrastructure and logistics network in Germany, including €8.8 billion for AWS data centres.
