item.title: South Sudan says Sudanese drone attack killed scores in Abyei market
item.description: South Sudanese officials said Sudan's military had carried out drone strikes that hit a market in the disputed Abyei region, killing about 73 people, the latest attack to cause mass casualties near Sudan's borders.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Sudanese officials said Sudan's military had carried out drone strikes that hit a market in the disputed Abyei region, killing about 73 people, the latest attack to cause mass casualties near Sudan's borders. Sudan has been [USN:L6N40Y0KB TEXT:"gripped by war"] between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) since April 2023, and the conflict has spilled over the country's borders, threatening to destabilise the region. Yohana Akol Ngor, the caretaker minister of information in Abyei, did not provide evidence for his claim of who was responsible for the attack, which according to local authorities took place around midday on Monday. A spokesperson for Sudan's armed forces did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the allegations. A diplomatic source and an aid worker told Reuters the strike hit a fuel depot in the market, with the diplomatic source saying the depot had been used in the past by the RSF to supply its forces. South Sudan declared independence from Sudan in 2011. Since then, both countries have staked a claim to oil-rich Abyei, which is jointly administered. It borders Sudan's Kordofan region, which has become a major centre of fighting in Sudan's war. That conflict has drawn in local militias and foreign powers and created what the United Nations has described as the world's worst humanitarian crisis. Officials in Sudan's military-led government told Reuters the RSF is active in parts of Abyei. Reuters could not immediately verify that assertion. The United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei (UNISFA) warned in May that the presence of the RSF in Abyei had increased insecurity there, adding that delays in determining the disputed region's final status had put civilians and UNISFA personnel at risk. STRUGGLE TO RETRIEVE BODIES Ngor told Reuters that emergency workers had struggled to retrieve the bodies because of fires caused by the strikes. "Around 73 people have been killed and 19 have been wounded ... a number of drones were shot yesterday by the Sudanese armed forces," Ngor said. South Sudan's foreign ministry said in a statement late Monday that drones struck a market located north of Abyei town, but did not specify the number of civilian casualties. The ministry said it had summoned the Sudanese ambassador to convey the government's "strong protest and deep concern regarding the attack and its implications for the security of civilians and the stability of the Abyei Area." The incident illustrates the lethality of airstrikes in Sudan's war, in which drone attacks [USN:L6N44V0K3 TEXT:"now dominate"], and the spread of the conflict around the country's borders. Sudanese armed forces and the RSF have recently escalated drone strikes, with a series of attacks targeting RSF-held Nyala and army-held Khartoum airport this week. Sudanese rights group Emergency Lawyers said dozens of people were killed in attacks on October 17 and 18 in al-Muglad in West Kordofan state, attributing them to the Sudanese army. Chadian authorities have accused Sudan’s military of carrying out drone strikes on its territory, which UN experts say is regularly used by RSF supply lines. Sudan's foreign ministry said in late August that its armed forces were acting to protect the country's security, "while respecting the sovereignty of its neighbours and without targeting their territory". On October 10, [USN:L1N45X06E TEXT:"an airstrike"] close to Sudan's border with Egypt killed more than 70 artisanal miners, according to a local rights group. PATIENTS TREATED FOR BURNS Abyei experiences frequent bouts of violence, with clashes usually involving rival ethnic groups or armed militias. The attack is the deadliest in years to hit the area, where medical supplies and healthcare are scarce. Medical charity Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) said in a statement posted late on Monday that it was treating more than 20 wounded people at the nearby Ameth Bek Hospital. "So far we received over 20 patients, including several critical cases. Patients with burns were also admitted. We are providing surgical services and wound dressing, along with other emergency care," said Christian Lindauer, MSF medical activities manager at Ameth Bek Hospital. Photographs shared on MSF's official social media account showed bandaged patients lying on the floor as they received care for their injuries. Last year, at least six Bangladeshi peacekeepers were killed and eight wounded in a [USN:L1N3XK016 TEXT:"drone attack"] by separatist armed groups on a UN base, Bangladesh's armed forces said.

item.title: AI worries weigh on ABB shares despite record orders
item.description: ABB dropped nearly 6% on Tuesday as market nervousness about the sustainability of investments in artificial intelligence weighed on the Swiss engineering company, which is a major supplier to data centres.
item.dc:creator: John Revill
item.content:encoded: ABB (ABBN.S) dropped nearly 6% on Tuesday as market nervousness about the sustainability of investments in artificial intelligence weighed on the Swiss engineering company, which is a major supplier to data centres. Record new orders and an increase in its full-year sales guidance failed to appease institutional buy-side investors who were looking for more, analysts said, as AI-linked stocks fell more broadly. On [USN:L1N46600F TEXT:"South Korea's stock market"], which has become one of the clearest measures of AI sentiment, traders sold heavily on Tuesday as concern mounted over rising costs. While European semiconductor stocks [USN:L8N4660GV TEXT:"also fell"], ABB shares fell more than peers. The stock, which reached its highest level to date of 89.14 Swiss francs ($108.13) in June, dropped to 70.72 Swiss francs on the Swiss exchange after the results. "Operationally ABB remains strong, but waning AI enthusiasm is creating headwinds," said Marco Estermann, an analyst at Luzerner Kantonalbank. "Ahead of the third quarter there was a risk that even results expectations would not be enough to support the share price." During its third quarter, ABB said its revenue rose 14% to $9.70 billion, slightly below analysts' forecasts of $9.74 billion in a company-gathered consensus. Operational earnings before interest, tax and amortisation jumped 24% to $2.03 billion in the three months to the end of September, slightly ahead of analyst forecasts for $2.0 billion. Another analyst said fears had increased about the number of companies that will survive in the artificial intelligence sector, concerns that drove selling in US cloud company [USN:L4N461208 TEXT:"CoreWeave"] (CRWV.O) last week. Research firm Gartner Inc expects that by 2030, 80% of neocloud providers will cease independent operations because they will fail to generate enough revenue to meet their debts building and managing data centres. "There is a feeling of insecurity and uncertainty in the market that even good numbers may not be good enough," said ZKB analyst Florian Sager. "People are worrying about the huge debts that the neoclouds are taking on to build their projects. Investors question whether these companies get the revenues they need in the future to survive,” he said. ABB however remained bullish on the future of data centres and CEO Morten Wierod said demand for its services had not slowed. Orders surged 40% to $12 billion in the three months ended September 30, with data centres the biggest driver. The company raised its full-year sales outlook and also announced a pending $495 million investment in a joint venture with Mitsubishi Electric. "We see a continued acceleration in the market when we're looking at the demand for the build-out of data centres," Wierod told reporters. "Data centres will be a growth market for many years," he added. ($1 = 0.8244 Swiss francs)

item.title: Volkswagen bet on Xpeng to save its China business. It's not going to plan
item.description: When Volkswagen turned to EV maker Xpeng in 2023 to help fix its flailing Chinese business, executives touted the partnership as a shortcut to developing cars tailored for China at the high speed of the local auto sector.
item.dc:creator: Ju-min Park, Christina Amann
item.content:encoded: When Volkswagen turned to EV maker Xpeng in 2023 to help fix its flailing Chinese business, executives touted the partnership as a shortcut to developing cars tailored for China at the high speed of the local auto sector. Three years later, the alliance’s first product exemplifies Volkswagen’s descent in the world’s largest car market. The ID. UNYX 08 electric SUV sold an average of 267 vehicles a month between its April launch and August, data from automotive consultancy ThinkerCar show. That’s a fraction of the 3,622 monthly sales Volkswagen initially aimed to achieve this year, according to company planning documents. The weak debut reflects Volkswagen’s battle to revive its fortunes in China, where it reigned for decades until 2022 as the top automaker. China represents the challenge at the heart of Volkswagen’s global crisis: A market that once contributed nearly 50% of group profits now accounts for about 10%. That stunning reversal has forced the company into the [USN:L8N4570XW TEXT:"biggest restructuring"] in its 89-year history. The UNYX 08 also highlights a persistent problem in Volkswagen's China strategy. Volkswagen (VOWG.DE) recognized the market’s shift toward higher-end technology and sought local partners to catch up. Yet the German automaker struggled to turn those bets into commercial success. This report is based on a Reuters review of previously unreported company documents and interviews with six people familiar with Volkswagen, including current and former executives and consultants. It shows the automaker's ambitions ran ahead of what its products, pricing and sales strategy could deliver. Volkswagen sold the UNYX 08 through a nascent and limited distribution network. The vehicle also struggled against newer, software-laden Chinese electric SUVs. Volkswagen didn’t comment on the sales forecasts in the documents. In a statement, the automaker said its partnership with Xpeng has delivered a new electric architecture to underpin locally made models and support faster vehicle development – a project it said was completed in a record 18 months. The UNYX 08 SUV and the related UNYX 09 sedan were additional outcomes of the tie-up, the company added. Xpeng (9868.HK) declined to comment. Problems with the UNYX 08 began with the vehicle itself. The car launched with a price tag of about $34,260. But similarly priced Chinese rivals offered more-sophisticated features. Xiaomi’s YU7 had an advanced sensor package; Zeekr's 7X offered fast charging. Xiaomi sold almost 57,000 YU7s and Zeekr sold more than 21,000 7Xs between April and August, compared with about 1,300 UNYX 08s, according to ThinkerCar. "Chinese customers ask: Why buy an expensive German car if they can get the technology much cheaper,” said Pedro Pacheco, vice president of research at Gartner. Stephen Reitman, an auto analyst at Bernstein, recalled that Volkswagen showed analysts computer renderings of the Xpeng-linked models in April 2024. "The next day we went to the Beijing auto show and you could basically see this kind of design already on the market," Reitman said. A distribution gamble compounded the product’s challenges, five people told Reuters. Volkswagen largely sold the UNYX 08 through a separate, new dealer network run by Volkswagen Anhui, an EV-focused venture, rather than the more than 3,000 dealerships Volkswagen operated with joint-venture partners FAW and SAIC (600104.SS) . Volkswagen Anhui’s far-smaller footprint meant many consumers were unaware the vehicle existed, two of the people said. Volkswagen said sales of the Anhui models, including the earlier UNYX 06 and 07, were growing. The unit had expanded its sales network to 166 outlets and was working with FAW-Volkswagen at selected dealerships, the company said, adding that this approach aimed to reach more customers. FAW and SAIC didn’t respond to questions. For Volkswagen, the Xpeng partnership follows a string of troubled ventures, missed opportunities and abandoned initiatives in China that spanned batteries, autonomous driving, charging infrastructure, software and even flying cars . Volkswagen was “too slow in building the competence they need today,” said Stefan Bratzel, founder and director of the Center of Automotive Management, a German research institute. The dilemma faces nearly every foreign automaker in China. Having fallen behind in software, batteries and vehicle platforms, foreign brands have turned to Chinese partners to stay in the game. Yet access to Chinese technology doesn’t guarantee they can match local rivals’ speed, execution or appeal with consumers. Chinese brands led by BYD and Geely have gained share by bringing software-rich vehicles to market faster and often at lower prices, forcing once-dominant rivals including Volkswagen and Toyota to [USN:L1N45707R TEXT:"fight for relevance"]. ANOTHER BIG BET Despite the UNYX 08’s weak reception, Volkswagen is setting similarly aggressive targets for its next model developed with Xpeng, the UNYX 09 sedan. The car is due to reach showrooms this month. Company product-planning documents earlier this year forecast average monthly sales of nearly 4,900 vehicles, with annual volume exceeding 90,000 by 2034. At Volkswagen, ambitious forecasts can be essential to securing approval for new models from Wolfsburg headquarters, which can incentivize managers to submit optimistic projections, according to two people familiar with its planning. Volkswagen initially expected to sell 32,600 UNYX 08s through the end of 2026 and 70,400 next year, the planning documents show. Those plans, made in 2024, show the automaker also expected annual sales of more than 120,000 vehicles later in the product cycle. But early this year, Volkswagen cut the 2026 projection by more than 60% to 12,300 vehicles, the documents show. It nevertheless forecast sales of 64,000 in 2027, about 10% below the initial target. In recent weeks, the company has been advertising the UNYX 08 at a 17% discount on the April launch price. ‘MARRIAGE AND DIVORCE’ Volkswagen saw the Chinese disruption coming. At a 2019 presentation for investors and shareholders, Volkswagen Group China said it was preparing nearly 40 locally produced new-energy vehicle models — EVs and plug-in hybrids — by 2025 and could deliver 1.5 million in China that year. It achieved less than one-tenth of that target, delivering 115,500 battery-electric vehicles in China last year, according to company data. As China's EV market accelerated, Volkswagen explored various local tie-ups, hoping to unlock the speed and expertise it lacked, according to three people, corporate records and public announcements. Two people familiar with Volkswagen's China partnerships said the company called this approach "marriage and divorce" – forming alliances with local companies to learn from them, then exiting once it had absorbed what it needed. Around the time Ralf Brandstaetter became Volkswagen China's chief executive in August 2022, the automaker explored cooperation with BYD – China’s largest EV maker – including potentially using BYD's Dolphin platform for the Jetta brand, according to two people. Those efforts haven’t been previously reported. During due diligence, Volkswagen staff examining BYD's finances were struck by the Chinese automaker's lower manufacturing costs, one of the people said. BYD (002594.SZ) wasn’t interested in collaborating, the two sources said. Reuters couldn’t establish why a deal didn’t happen. The Chinese EV maker would seize Volkswagen’s crown as China’s sales leader in 2023. That same year, Volkswagen also explored a partnership with Leapmotor (9863.HK) , according to the two people. Stellantis (STLAM.MI) ultimately [USN:L4N3BV66D TEXT:"struck a deal"] with Leapmotor later that year. Volkswagen declined to comment publicly before publication on Reuters’ reporting about possible partnerships with BYD and Leapmotor. After the story was published, Volkswagen denied having any discussions with BYD regarding collaboration. BYD didn’t comment, while Leapmotor didn’t respond to questions. Some partnerships that did materialize generated new problems rather than solving old ones. Reuters reported in July that Volkswagen's canceled flying-car project had become mired in legal disputes with a Chinese partner. A venture with Chinese startup Du-Power to build fast-charging stations also went awry. The tie-up, launched in 2020, ended in shareholder disputes, litigation and supplier complaints alleging unpaid bills, corporate filings show. In 2024, the startup sued Volkswagen China and the venture’s executives and directors, alleging harm to its business interests. Volkswagen told Reuters that China’s Supreme People’s Court dismissed the startup’s claims in March. Neither Du-Power nor the court responded to questions. ‘EXCEPTIONAL’ CONTRACTION In some ways, Volkswagen’s predicament illustrates the success of China's industrial policy. In exchange for market access, Volkswagen tied up with Chinese automakers, shared technology and invested — only to be outsold by local players. Those checkered bets are now colliding with a market in convulsion after years of breakneck growth. In a September 10 message to staff reviewed by Reuters, Brandstaetter described an industry facing an "exceptional" contraction. He said Volkswagen expected China’s passenger-car market to [USN:P8N43T0CN TEXT:"shrink by 20% this year"], or about 4.5 million vehicles. Brandstaetter said industry profit margins had fallen to 1.5%, product cycles had compressed from seven years to three, and new EV models were seeing steep sales declines after three months. Volkswagen, he wrote, must urgently "align our production capacities with market realities" and eliminate "unnecessary duplication" among China brands and entities — a reckoning with a crisis years in the making. In 2019, one in five passenger cars sold in China was a Volkswagen. In the first eight months of this year, the group’s share had fallen to 10%, according to the China Passenger Car Association. What distinguishes Volkswagen’s plight is its deep dependence on China and its struggle to execute a decisive transformation in a market now dominated by Chinese companies. That made its Xpeng bet pivotal. One former Volkswagen figure compared its predicament to that faced by Nokia, Kodak and BlackBerry: The automaker’s leadership assumed its brands would endure, even as the market shifted toward Chinese competitors with superior technology and faster innovation cycles. Bill Russo, founder of Shanghai-based advisory firm Automobility, sees the comparison as a useful warning but not yet a verdict. Volkswagen still has a path to recovery, he said. The risk, he added, “is that the market moves faster than the company can reinvent itself.”

item.title: Indonesia battles to stabilise market after MSCI expulsion threat
item.description: Indonesian stocks rose on Tuesday as authorities in Jakarta introduced measures to restrict selling after a record two-day $82 billion rout sparked by index provider MSCI's warning of possible removal from its global indexes.
item.dc:creator: Ankur Banerjee, Stefanno Sulaiman
item.content:encoded: Indonesian stocks rose on Tuesday as authorities in Jakarta introduced measures to restrict selling after a [USN:L1N46500W TEXT:"record two-day"] $82 billion rout sparked by index provider MSCI's [USN:L4N46509U TEXT:"warning"] of possible [USN:L6N4620Z3 TEXT:"removal"] from its global indexes. Jakarta's benchmark index (.JKSE) advanced 5.3%, after hitting a six-year low in the previous session as the world's worst-performing stock market this year dropped 14.8% over Friday and Monday. The index is down about 40% this year. The selloff was sparked by MSCI's [USN:L4N46124S TEXT:"warning"] on Friday that Indonesia could be reclassified as a "[USN:L6N46208E TEXT:"standalone"]" market from "emerging markets", a harsher-than-expected downgrade that stunned investors and policymakers and raised fears of large-scale passive fund outflows. The index provider cited Indonesia's failure to improve ownership transparency and curb coordinated trading, turning what had been a downgrade risk to "frontier" market status into a full-blown crisis of investor confidence. Relegation to "standalone" status would mark a major setback for Southeast Asia's biggest economy as investors grow increasingly uneasy about the country's fiscal health and the autonomy of its central bank under President Prabowo Subianto. Foreign investors have already pulled nearly $5 billion from Indonesian equities this year, with Goldman Sachs estimating a removal by MSCI could spur $5.6 billion of passive outflows. After an online meeting with MSCI on Monday, the Indonesia Stock Exchange said it would exclude from its benchmark index any stocks with a high concentration of ownership by any person or entity. "We are doing what is best for our market," IDX President Director Jeffrey Hendrik said, adding the exclusion would provide a more accurate picture of the index's movements. He said the affected stocks account for roughly 18% of the total index weight. Gary Tan, portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments, said excluding tightly held stocks should help address some investability concerns, but implementation would be key, given the potential for domestic pushback. "From here, we think the bigger incremental risk to flows is likely to come from active rather than passive funds," he said. EYES ON CENTRAL BANK MSCI's warning has weighed on the rupiah , which strengthened slightly to 17,980 per US dollar on Tuesday but remained close to the record low of 18,190 hit in June ahead of a policy decision from Indonesia's central bank. Bank Indonesia is expected to hold rates steady on Wednesday, although some economists have raised the prospect of a rate hike to defend the currency, which is down 7% this year. George Xu, a director in Fitch Ratings' sovereigns team, said the latest concerns and substantial market selloff reinforced the risks the rating agency identified when it [USN:L1N3ZS06T TEXT:"revised the outlook"] on Indonesia to negative in March. "From sovereign rating perspective, we do not anticipate the consultation announcement itself to have material immediate credit implications," he said, but added that external pressure could raise the government’s borrowing costs and erode external buffers. "PLEASE PRAY," WATCHDOG URGES AMID INVESTOR UNEASE To stem the rout, the stock exchange this week halved the daily down limit on stock prices to 7% from 15%, while setting a 1 rupiah down limit on shares priced at 14 rupiah or less. Market watchers said the move to remove stocks with highly concentrated ownership from the benchmark index was a constructive step, but noted investors would still have some exposure to those firms through direct ownership and investment products such as mutual funds. "We must ensure that even if a stock is delisted from the Jakarta Composite Index, concentration risk does not continue to accumulate within products purchased by the public," said Liza Camelia Suryanata, head of research at stockbroker Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia. Also on Monday, Prabowo held talks with finance chiefs, including the head of the Financial Services Authority (OJK), the finance minister and the BI governor. After the meeting, OJK chief Friderica Widyasari Dewi said the regulator would continue to advance Indonesia's capital market reforms, particularly regarding transparency, liquidity, and law enforcement against various forms of violations. "The stock market has started to rebound today; the important thing is to keep building confidence," said OJK's Friderica in a separate event. "I haven't had a moment's rest since Friday. Please pray that we can get through this successfully."

item.title: Gavin McKenna, 18, nets winning goal as Maple Leafs top Sharks
item.description: Rookie Gavin McKenna netted the game-winning goal as the Toronto Maple Leafs beat the San Jose Sharks 3-1 on Monday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Rookie Gavin McKenna netted the game-winning goal as the Toronto Maple Leafs beat the San Jose Sharks 3-1 on Monday night. McKenna gave the Maple Leafs a 2-1 lead 4:56 into the final frame, receiving the puck from Auston Matthews on the outside and enjoying a relatively unimpeded path toward goal. The 18-year-old was allowed to stroll forward and ping it in off the post for his first NHL power-play goal in his 10th game. The game marked the first encounter between McKenna and Ivar Stenberg, the highly touted top two picks of the 2026 NHL Draft. McKenna was selected first overall out of Penn State, just ahead of Stenberg, who previously played in his native Sweden. Mason Marchment scored in the first period for San Jose before Matthews tied the game with 12 seconds remaining in the second period. Matthews added two assists for his fourth multi-point game of the young season. Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 30 shots in his first home win as a Maple Leaf. Yaroslav Askarov made 29 saves for the visitors. Toronto snapped a three-game losing streak (0-2-1), while San Jose fell to 1-3-1 in its past five games. Marchment opened the scoring 13:54 in. Tyler Toffoli snatched up Toronto's clearing attempt at the point and flipped the puck to Marchment lurking behind the play. The former Maple Leaf pulled the puck out of the air and shoveled it over a sprawling Bobrovsky. The Sharks were able to kill off a 58-second five-on-three toward the end of the first period after Jacob Trouba and Dmitry Orlov were called for consecutive tripping penalties. Matthews tied the game 1-1 at the end of the second period on what was Toronto's fourth power play. Kirill Marchenko spun away from Trouba in the corner and slipped the puck to the captain, who ripped in a powerful one-timer from one knee. Macklin Celebrini was responsible for the penalty after jumping onto the ice too early, resulting in a too-many-men call. Nick Paul sealed the deal on an empty-net goal with less than 40 seconds remaining from just inside the offensive zone. The Sharks are one of two teams still without a regulation win on the season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Australian barber hailed as hero for running to lawmaker's rescue during attack
item.description: Australian barber Ricky Jefferies has been hailed as a hero for running out of his store to detain a man who authorities allege deliberately drove a car into lawmaker Helen Haines in the small town of Wangaratta, an incident that has shocked the country.
item.dc:creator: Christine Chen
item.content:encoded: Australian barber Ricky Jefferies has been hailed as a hero for running out of his store to detain a man who authorities allege deliberately drove a car into lawmaker Helen Haines in the small town of Wangaratta, an incident that has shocked the country. Jefferies had just finished haircuts for a young family on Monday when he said he heard a "loud bang" outside his shop and realised the driver of a Toyota LandCruiser had [USN:L1N46508R TEXT:"struck Haines, "]leaving her badly injured. "It was crazy, I just ran out the front to see what was happening," he told reporters on Tuesday. He said he ran to assist the well-respected local MP, grabbing a knife from the alleged attacker's pocket and pulling him out of the car. "He did have a knife. He didn't pull it out. I just wasn't comfortable with his movements, and so I basically just took it out of his pocket and threw it away," he said. Jefferies said he then held the man down until police arrived. "I just leant over him and once he was on the ground and he was no longer a threat, I just stood with him and I told him that he can't leave," he said. Haines, 65, was airlifted to hospital where she underwent surgery overnight. She [USN:L1N46510F TEXT:"remains in a critical condition"]. Early investigations suggested the driver, identified as a 43-year-old man, performed a U-turn before hitting Haines as she was loading or unloading things from the trunk of her car, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said. Counterterrorism authorities are among the multiple agencies involved in the investigation. While police have given no motive for the alleged attack, the involvement of counterterrorism investigators has raised alarm that it could have been an act of political violence, which is rare in Australia. Jefferies, whose shop is next door to Haines' electorate office around three hours' drive northeast of Melbourne, described the former midwife as a "genuine, kind person". Albanese praised Jefferies' intervention, calling him a hero. "At this dark and terrible time, an element of light is the fact that a Good Samaritan, someone rushed to Helen's defence in Wangaratta, put themselves potentially at risk by doing so. And that person is a hero today," Albanese said in an interview with the Nine network's "Today" show. Jefferies downplayed the praise. "I don't think I'm a hero. I think that I just was a person who had an opportunity to intervene in a safe-ish sort of way," he said.

item.title: Mobile wallet operator GCash parent Mynt ends flat after record Philippine IPO
item.description: Fintech firm Mynt , operator of mobile wallet GCash, ended flat on its first day of trade market after raising around $967 million in the largest-ever IPO in the Philippines, marking a steadier debut than recent regional technology listings.
item.dc:creator: Yantoultra Ngui, Karen Lema, Roshan Thomas
item.content:encoded: Fintech firm Mynt (GCASH.PS) , operator of mobile wallet GCash, ended flat on its first day of trade market after raising around $967 million in the largest-ever IPO in the Philippines, marking a steadier debut than recent regional technology listings. The stock opened at 6.60 pesos per share, in line with its offer price, and rose as much as 2.4% to 6.76 pesos before closing at 6.60 pesos. The closing price valued Mynt at about 442 billion pesos ($7 billion), making it one of the country's largest listed companies. "Mynt's flat debut is a plausible outcome given the development of regional listings," said Ke Yan, head of research at Singapore-based Shenton Research. "Issuers have to balance valuation against getting the money raised to get the deal done." Mynt's IPO and market debut comes amid a recent [USN:L1N46605X TEXT:"broader selloff"] in AI-related shares globally, which saw some IPOs getting pulled or [USN:FWN4660V7 TEXT:"delayed"], and investors becoming more selective. Firmus [USN:L1N45U12T TEXT:"pulled its Australian IPO"], while AirTrunk [USN:L4N45Z0H4 TEXT:"delayed its planned Singapore REIT listing"]. South Korean AI firm Elice [USN:L1N46600F TEXT:"fell sharply on its debut"], while [USN:L1N45V02W TEXT:"Eswin"] and [USN:L1N461058 TEXT:"Transsion"], which listed in Hong Kong this month, closed below their offer prices on their first day of trade. Mynt's IPO, which raised 60.9 billion pesos after including an overallotment option, surpassed Monde Nissin's (MONDE.PS) 52.2-billion-peso IPO in 2021 to become the Philippines biggest-ever IPO, according to LSEG data. In a Tuesday [USN:FWN4660UZ TEXT:"stock exchange filing"], stabilising agent UBS said it may purchase up to 1.204 billion overallotment shares in the open market during the stabilisation period, which ends no more than 30 days from the listing date. Global investors including BlackRock, Citadel and Fidelity International bought Mynt shares in the IPO, in what analysts say, would be a boost for a Southeast Asian market, which has struggled to attract foreign investments. The Philippine stock market index is down 4.08% so far this year, and foreign investors sold 20.86 billion pesos worth of shares from January to August, a PSE monthly report showed . Mynt President and CEO Martha Sazon said the listing marked a new stage in the company's effort to broaden access to financial services for Filipinos who have long been outside the formal banking system. Nearly 90% of GCash customers come from low- to middle-income households, she said. BIGGEST IN THE PHILIPPINES Mynt, backed by Globe Telecom (GLO.PS) , Ant Group and Ayala Corp (AC.PS) , owns GCash, the Philippines' largest finance app, according to its prospectus. The platform offers payments, money transfers, lending, savings, investments and insurance products. The domestic market-focused company had 41.5 million monthly active users in the three-month period that ended on June 30, or nearly 56% of the Philippines' adult population, according to its IPO prospectus. GCash users completed payment transactions worth 9.84 trillion pesos in the first half of 2026. "It is a record and, more importantly, a statement of confidence in Mynt, in the Philippine economy and in the strength of our capital market," Philippine Stock Exchange President and CEO Ramon Monzon said. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said the listing came at a time when the stock market needed renewed investor interest and broader participation, adding that attracting fresh capital remained a challenge. He said strong demand from local and international investors offered a "reason for optimism" and reflected continued confidence in Filipino enterprises. Mynt sold 8.03 billion shares at 6.60 pesos each. Mynt plans to use the proceeds to fund growth in its digital financial services business, product development and general corporate purposes, according to its prospectus. Mynt said that for the six months ending June 30, its net income rose 7.3% from a year earlier to 10.82 billion pesos. Revenue rose 10.4% to 43.27 billion pesos. Morgan Stanley, JP Morgan and UBS acted as joint global coordinators and joint bookrunners for the IPO, while Jefferies, CLSA and HSBC were international joint bookrunners. BPI Capital and BDO Capital served as domestic lead underwriters and joint bookrunners. ($1 = 62.9790 Philippine pesos)

item.title: Gold eases as higher oil prices stoke inflation concerns
item.description: Gold edged lower on Tuesday as rising oil prices stoked inflation concerns, with investors looking to next week's Federal Reserve meeting for clues on the US interest-rate outlook.
item.dc:creator: Vishak Mathew
item.content:encoded: Gold edged lower on Tuesday as rising oil prices stoked inflation concerns, with investors looking to next week's Federal Reserve meeting for clues on the US interest-rate outlook. Spot gold fell 0.5% to $4,120.49 per ounce by 0909 GMT. US gold futures for December delivery dropped 0.5% to $4,139.10 per ounce. "Persistent inflationary pressures, driven by high energy prices, continue to support expectations of further monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve," said Ricardo Evangelista, ActivTrades director and CEO. Oil prices advanced on Tuesday, with Brent hovering around a five-month high as traders priced in a geopolitical risk premium from Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf. "The Fed is widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged in October, so the main focus will be on its guidance regarding a possible increase in December," Evangelista added. Recent comments from [USN:L6N462084 TEXT:"Fed"] officials signalling little [USN:L1N4600EO TEXT:"urgency"] for further policy tightening have tempered expectations of a rate hike at the central bank's October 27-28 policy meeting, but traders see a 90% chance of a hike in December, according to CME's FedWatch Tool. Although gold is traditionally considered an inflation hedge, higher rates dent its appeal as investors prefer yield-bearing assets. The US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE), the central bank's preferred inflation gauge, due next week is also on investors' radar for clues on the interest-rate outlook. Elsewhere in Japan, central bank Governor Kazuo Ueda [USN:L1N465004 TEXT:"said"] underlying inflation was "quite close" to the 2% target, signalling scope for further rate hikes. Among other metals, spot silver rose 0.2% to $57.1931 per ounce, platinum fell 0.1% to $1,639.45 per ounce and palladium dropped 0.9% to $1,110.06 per ounce.

item.title: Australian lawmaker loses leg after vehicle attack being probed by anti-terror police
item.description: Doctors have amputated the leg of an Australian lawmaker after a man rammed her with his car and then reversed to hit her a second time, local media and officials said on Tuesday, in an incident being investigated by anti-terrorism police.
item.dc:creator: Renju Jose
item.content:encoded: Doctors have amputated the leg of an Australian lawmaker after a man rammed her with his car and then reversed to hit her a second time, local media and officials said on Tuesday, in an incident being investigated by anti-terrorism police. Helen Haines, an independent, underwent surgery overnight and remained in critical condition after Monday's attack in the small rural town of Wangaratta, north of Melbourne. The motive for the attack has yet to be revealed, but Australia’s prime minister has linked it to a climate of ugly, polarised political debate in the country. "It's clear that there was a deliberate act here. This wasn't an accident, someone just skidding off the road," Albanese told ABC News. Early investigations suggested the car hit Haines as she was loading or unloading things from the trunk of her car, he said. Australian media, citing unidentified sources, reported Haines had lost one leg as a result of her injuries and that doctors were working to save the other leg. A 43-year-old man was arrested following the attack, with counter-terrorism authorities among the multiple agencies involved in the investigation. Police are considering potential charges, including causing harm to a public official - an offence that carries a maximum penalty of 10 years' imprisonment - as they work to establish a motive for the attack. "At this stage it appears this is an isolated incident," Australian Federal Police Commissioner Krissy Barrett said. STRUCK TWO TIMES Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke told ABC Radio that witnesses said the alleged attacker reversed the vehicle and struck Haines a second time before a bystander intervened. Ricky Jefferies ran from his barber shop, restraining the attacker and removing a knife from him after initially believing the incident was a car accident, Australian media reported. "I heard a loud bang with no brakes. It was crazy, I just ran out to the front to see what's happening," Jefferies told reporters outside his shop. "I didn't realise the seriousness of the situation initially, and once it became relevant I just did what I could and what others were already trying to do." 'TURN TEMPERATURE DOWN' Violent attacks on politicians are extremely rare in Australia, where federal lawmakers, state leaders and even prime ministers are regularly seen in supermarkets and coffee shops, attending community events and chatting with voters with minimal security. [USN:L4N4650NF TEXT:"Haines"] worked in nursing and midwifery and as an academic before being elected to parliament as an independent in 2019 in the seat of Indi. She retained the seat in 2022 and 2025. Outside the hospital where Haines is being treated, Melbourne resident Shawn Hill said the attack showed that "the political climate is becoming more and more polarising today." "No one deserves to be put at risk of anything, especially someone who is serving the people and trying to do what is best for the Australian community," Hill told Reuters. Albanese urged Australians to engage more respectfully with one another, expressing concern about growing division in the country. He also noted a "significant increase" in threats against politicians in recent years. "We all have a responsibility to turn the temperature down," Albanese said. "I really don't want to see the character of Australia change."

item.title: Trump's approval falls to record low of 31% as midterms near, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
item.description: President Donald Trump's approval rating fell to a record low.
item.dc:creator: Jason Lange
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump's approval rating fell to a record low as Americans worried about high gasoline prices and appeared ready to punish his Republican Party in the November 3 congressional elections , according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll that closed on Monday. Some 31% of Americans approve of Trump's performance in office, down a percentage point from two weeks earlier and the lowest level in either of his presidential terms, the four-day poll showed. Asked which party they would vote for if the congressional elections were held today in what is known as a "generic ballot" question, some 47% of registered voters in the nationwide poll picked Democrats and 35% chose Republicans. The 12-point Democratic advantage was the widest over the current election cycle and could bolster Democratic hopes of seizing control of the US House of Representatives and the US Senate. For Republicans, losing control of either chamber could complicate Trump's agenda in the last two years of his term. Generic ballot polls are national polls that provide an overall view of which party poll respondents want to see in charge in Congress. While these polls provide a view of national public sentiment, they do not capture all the nuances of the state-by-state and district-by-district contests that determine control of the Senate and House, contests in which Republicans hold some structural advantages. A Reuters/Ipsos poll two weeks earlier showed Democrats leading Republicans by 7 points, 44% to 37%. Much of the drop in support for Republican congressional candidates was due to a larger share of women saying they would pick Democrats. Some 50% of female voters said they would vote Democratic, compared to 32% eyeing Republican candidates. Men also favored Democrats, but by a smaller margin. Trump's popularity has suffered since he ordered military strikes on Iran in February alongside US ally Israel. The war triggered a surge in gasoline prices, hitting household finances. Some 68% of Americans disapprove of Trump's handling of the economy, including 37% of self-identified Republicans. Voters in the poll picked Democrats over Republicans as the better stewards of the economy, by 40% to 33%. The survey, which was conducted online, gathered responses from 1,679 US adults, including 1,279 registered voters. The poll's results had a margin of error of 2 percentage points for all respondents and 3 points for registered voters.

item.title: Residents winched from rooftops as torrential rain hits eastern Spain
item.description: Helicopters rescued people stranded on rooftops as torrential rains swept across eastern Spain on Monday, as floods and storms killed at least three people and shelter-in-place orders remained in force for more than 80,000 residents.
item.dc:creator: Eva Mañez
item.content:encoded: Helicopters rescued people stranded on rooftops as torrential rains swept across eastern Spain on Monday, as floods and storms killed at least three people and shelter-in-place orders remained in force for more than 80,000 residents. The downpour from Storm Adam cut off several towns along the Mediterranean coast as rivers burst their banks and streets turned into torrents, leaving scenes reminiscent of the [USN:L8N3W10M6 TEXT:"catastrophic flooding"] that killed more than 230 people in the Valencia region two years ago. Members of the Military Emergencies Unit found the body of a woman in the town of Oliva during rescue operations on Monday, bringing the death toll to three, regional broadcaster A Punt reported, citing sources from the unit. Two other women were confirmed dead over the weekend: one whose body was washed up on a beach in Sagunto, in the eastern region of Valencia, and another who was [USN:L8N464012 TEXT:"swept away by floodwaters"] in Cabrera de Mar, near Barcelona. 'IT'S A DISASTER' In Els Poblets, northeast of Alicante, cars and vans were piled on top of one another from the force of the water as residents tried to salvage what they could from their homes. “The village, well, it's a disaster. Some people have lost everything all over again, just like in 2007, when exactly the same thing happened," chef Javier Fornez, 49, said. Meteorologists say human-driven climate change makes such [USN:L8N3M628P TEXT:"extreme weather events"] more frequent and destructive. National weather agency AEMET said torrential rains linked to Storm Adam dumped exceptional amounts of rain across eastern Spain, with Pego, in Alicante province, recording 632 mm (25 inches) in 36 hours, while several locations in southern Valencia and northern Alicante exceeded 500 mm over the same period. AEMET issued several red alerts, warning local people to avoid all travel and to seek higher ground. On Monday morning, 800,000 residents were under shelter-in-place orders, but that had been reduced to 87,000 in eight municipalities by late afternoon. HEAVY-DUTY VEHICLES STRUGGLE TO ACCESS SOME AREAS More than 2,000 people were evacuated, mainly in Oliva, and authorities carried out nearly 100 rescues in Valencia and Alicante, the Civil Guard police said. The mayor of Pego, Enrique Moll, told A Punt radio that several people were still waiting to be evacuated by helicopter from their roofs. All access routes to the town were blocked and even heavy-duty military vehicles were unable to move forward in some areas, he added. The deputy mayor of the coastal town of Oliva, Salvador Llopis, told state broadcaster TVE on Monday that emergency services were rescuing trapped residents, particularly elderly people stuck inside their homes with water up to their waists. "They have to stay on top of tables and furniture to avoid getting wet," he said, adding that the rains had started to ease after causing extensive damage to infrastructure. More than 100,000 students in Valencia region have had classes suspended due to the alerts, while the central government has deployed emergency units from the military and national police. The focus of the storm was expected to shift to Catalonia on Monday afternoon, especially Barcelona and Girona provinces, where more than 100 mm of rain could fall in less than 12 hours. Authorities warned that the risk was heightened because the soil was already saturated from previous storms.

item.title: Alberta votes to remain part of Canada
item.description: Alberta residents voted to remain part of Canada in the province's first-ever referendum on separation, in a much-needed win for Prime Minister Mark Carney as he attempts to unify the country amid a trade war with the US.
item.dc:creator: Amanda Stephenson, Maria Cheng
item.content:encoded: Alberta residents voted to remain part of Canada in the province's first-ever referendum on [USN:L6N3Z2101 TEXT:"separation"], in a much-needed win for Prime Minister Mark Carney as he attempts to unify the country amid a [USN:SPN44J009 TEXT:"trade war"] with the US. CBC News, Canada's government-funded national broadcaster, called the result late Monday after 33% of the vote had been counted. At the time of the call, 76% of tallied votes were in support of the "remain" side versus 23% in favor of the province moving forward with a binding vote on separation. The [USN:L6N46019J TEXT:"referendum"] was nonbinding. "Albertans made a clear choice," Prime Minister Mark Carney said in a statement. "They chose unity, to build together, and to take care of each other." "Canada is greater than the sum of its parts," he said. Pollsters and analysts had repeatedly dismissed the possibility of a separatist victory, citing data that showed about one-third of residents in the western province supported a future referendum on leaving. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith announced the referendum in May, saying it was “time to have a vote, understand the will of Albertans on this subject, and move on.” Late Monday, Smith issued a statement on social media saying she was "very pleased" that early results show widespread support for remaining in Canada. She said she would address Albertans on Tuesday to discuss the results and "where our province goes from here." A small but vocal group of separatists has campaigned for months for an independent Alberta, arguing that the province’s energy wealth is subsidizing poorer parts of Canada and that Alberta would be far richer without Ottawa bureaucracy impeding its path. Last week, Carney told a rally in Calgary that voting to leave Canada would be “a dangerous bluff that will lead to years of deep division,” and appealed to Albertans to “vote like Canada depends on it.” Carney, who grew up mostly in Alberta, acknowledged that Albertans have often felt slighted by Ottawa and said his government had approved a proposed [USN:L1N45N0PP TEXT:"new pipeline"], adding that Alberta is critical to helping Canada reduce its dependence on the US. Alberta's referendum follows two previous referendums on separation in the majority French-speaking province of Quebec. Quebecers voted to stay in Canada in both instances. First Nations groups have also [USN:L6N41R10Y TEXT:"objected"] to the idea of an independent Alberta, as their land treaties with Ottawa predate the province’s creation within Canada. CBC News reported strong turnout from First Nations. One southern Alberta polling station in an area that is home to the Siksika Nation temporarily ran out of ballots, and then stayed open until after 10 p.m. MT (0400 GMT) to ensure everyone in line had the chance to vote. Still, Monday’s referendum is unlikely to end the separatist movement in Alberta. Before the referendum, some separatist leaders said they would continue to pursue another vote even if most Albertans voted to remain. According to data released on October 16 by the pollster Angus Reid, 62% of Albertans believe “there will never be an end to the separatist movement” in the province. Alberta's referendum also included [USN:L6N3ZF146 TEXT:"nine other nonbinding questions"] on topics including immigration, access to provincial services — such as education, social care and healthcare — and voter identification requirements. Results for those questions were still trickling in.

item.title: Airlines cancel flights to Saudi Arabia after Riyadh airport attacks
item.description: Airlines are cancelling flights to Saudi Arabia following the deadly attacks on Riyadh airport by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis earlier in October, extending disruption to air travel across the region.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Airlines are cancelling flights to Saudi Arabia following the [USN:L1N45X01E TEXT:"deadly attacks"] on Riyadh airport by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis earlier in October, extending disruption to air travel across the region. The airport reopened on Saturday, but airlines are required to seek permission from Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority for any departures or landings. Here is a list of measures taken by airlines in alphabetical order: AIR FRANCE-KLM (AIRF.PA) The Franco-Dutch group has extended its previous suspension of services to and from the Saudi capital up to and including November 7, while flights to Dubai remain suspended up to and including October 31. AIR INDIA The Indian carrier has extended the suspension of flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah until October 24. AKASA AIR (SNVA.NS) The Mumbai-based budget carrier has suspended flights to and from Jeddah and Riyadh through October 27. CATHAY PACIFIC (0293.HK) The Hong Kong flag carrier postponed the resumption of its Hong Kong–Dubai and Hong Kong–Riyadh routes through January 31, 2027. DELTA (DAL.N) The US airline will delay its planned flights from Atlanta to Riyadh until March 2027. It also issued a travel waiver allowing passengers to change or cancel their flights to, from and through Riyadh from October 23 to March 27. ETIHAD AIRWAYS The Abu Dhabi-based carrier cancelled all flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh and between Abu Dhabi and Dammam through October 24. item.title: Record Chinese turnout puts European carmakers under pressure at Paris show
item.description: A record 20 Chinese car brands will descend on next week's Paris Motor Show, underscoring how rapidly China's automakers have established themselves as a competitive threat in Europe despite mounting trade barriers.
item.dc:creator: Nick Carey, Giulio Piovaccari
item.content:encoded: (This Oct 9 story has been refiled to add a dropped letter from Brad Kuntz's last name in paragraph 5.) A record 20 Chinese car brands will descend on next week's Paris Motor Show, underscoring how rapidly China's automakers have established themselves as a competitive threat in Europe despite mounting trade barriers. European carmakers will use the show to unveil new models and try to reassure investors they can compete, as Chinese rivals gain market share with a growing range of electric vehicles and hybrids. This year's Chinese contingent will be twice the size of the one at the last show in 2024, with established names such as BYD (002594.SZ) and Chery (9973.HK) joined by newcomers including Aito and Avatr. The Paris Motor Show comes at a pivotal moment for Europe's auto industry. Sales by European manufacturers in China have slumped since the COVID-19 pandemic, while Chinese automakers, largely shut out of the US and facing weaker [USN:L4N4490F1 TEXT:"demand"] at home, have increasingly turned their attention to Europe. "The Chinese are saying 'we've got to try and dominate Europe because we can't do anything in the US'," said Brad Kuntz, a partner at consultancy Grant Thornton Stax. "If the US had allowed Chinese automakers in, Europe ... wouldn't be so much of a battleground." Data from Schmidt Automotive Research show Chinese brands held a 10.7% share of the European market in the second quarter, up from 5.7% a year earlier and above Japanese rivals who arrived in Europe in the 1970s. EUROPEAN CARMAKERS PLAY A 'DOUBLE GAME' Pressure from Chinese competition, alongside weak European demand, US tariffs and the costs of electrification, is starting to tell on European automakers. Volkswagen is [USN:L8N44W0B8 TEXT:"cutting thousands of jobs"] and considering factory closures to slash costs, while luxury rival BMW (BMWG.DE) is also shedding thousands of workers. The European Union imposed tariffs on Chinese-made fully electric cars two years ago, but Chinese automakers have responded by expanding into combustion-engine models and plug-in hybrids. Chinese brands accounted for more than 26% of the Western European plug-in hybrid market in the second quarter, up from just 2.2% in the same period two years earlier. Europe's auto industry is now pushing for [USN:L1N44I0MW TEXT:"tariffs on Chinese"] plug-in hybrids, while the EU is working on legislation that will include "Made in Europe" provisions requiring minimum local content levels for EVs to qualify for key subsidies or government contracts. While battling Chinese rivals for market share, European automakers are also seeking to benefit from their rise by selling them capacity at underutilised factories and tapping into their EV technology. Stellantis (STLAM.MI) , for example, has partnered with China's state-owned [USN:FWN41W0RF TEXT:"Dongfeng"] (600006.SS) . "The Europeans are playing a sort of double game," said Pedro Pacheco, vice president of research at Gartner. 'STILL STRONG AND STILL READY' Chinese automakers have emerged as formidable competitors in EV technology, but European manufacturers are seeking to fight back with a new generation of more affordable electric models. "This motor show will probably be the most important one in the region since the pandemic," said automotive analyst Felipe Munoz. "This is the platform the Europeans are using to tell the Chinese they're still strong and still ready." One of the headline European launches at the show, Stellantis' revival of the Citroen 2CV, will test new rules allowing carmakers to cut back on some features in order to offer more affordable EVs and counter Chinese competition. Meanwhile, previously little-known Chinese brands such as Aito, the premium marque owned by Chongqing-based carmaker Seres Group (601127.SS) , will be looking for a breakthrough. Aito wants overseas sales to account for 20% of total volumes within three years, up from less than 1% currently, and plans to launch four premium electric SUVs for Europe in Paris. Francois Roudier, secretary-general of the International Organisation of Motor Vehicle Manufacturers, said the arrival of Chinese brands had helped reinvigorate motor shows after interest from some traditional manufacturers waned. The large turnout in Paris reflects growing pressure on automakers on both sides to compete for buyers in an increasingly crowded market, he said. "For years people were buying cars, now manufacturers have to sell them," he said, adding that manufacturers who did not attend "have made a mistake". "It's no show, no sell in a way."

item.title: French maize output to halve to 50-year low after drought, growers say
item.description: French grain maize output is on track to halve this year to 7 million metric tons, after lower sowings and record hot, dry weather ravaged crops, maize farmers' group AGPM said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: French grain maize output is on track to halve this year to 7 million metric tons, after lower sowings and record hot, dry weather ravaged crops, maize farmers' group AGPM said on Tuesday. That would be the lowest level since 1976 and compares to 13.7 million tons harvested last year, it said. "The worst has happened," AGPM Chairman Franck Laborde told reporters, blaming the fall on climate change-driven heatwaves and France's limits on water storage, which kept farmers from using water that could have been collected during an exceptionally rainy winter. France has suffered one of its worst hot and dry spells on record, with record temperatures in most parts of the country between May and August damaging crops, pastures and water supplies. The crisis prompted the government to issue a €1.3 billion [USN:L8N44W0F6 TEXT:"aid package"], and pledge to expand agricultural water storage. But Laborde said further help was needed or many farmers would not sow grains ahead of next season. "Without immediate cash flow, there will be no next season," he said. The fall in maize output would cut the sector's sales by €2.5 billion ($2.8 billion), with a further impact on villages where agriculture is the main source of income, Laborde said. The extremely dry weather mainly affected non-irrigated crops, which usually account for about a third of grain maize output, and the damage pushed a large share of the crop into feed-grade grain, Aude Cerrera from crop institute Arvalis said. The collapse in maize production will also lead to France importing significant amounts of maize this season, for the first time ever, notably from Brazil and Ukraine. European feed makers group [USN:L8N44U16T TEXT:"FEFAC"] last month estimated that drought across Europe would force the European Union to import an additional 7 million metric tons of maize in the 2026/27 season. ($1 = 0.8906 euros)

item.title: How France's 2027 budget battle could play out
item.description: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu's minority government faces a particularly treacherous budget season as opposition parties dig in for a fight over his deficit-cutting plans before an April-May presidential election.
item.dc:creator: Leigh Thomas
item.content:encoded: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu's minority government faces a particularly [USN:L8N44I0JF TEXT:"treacherous budget season"] as opposition parties dig in for a fight over his deficit-cutting plans before an April-May presidential election. The government is struggling to rein in its strained finances, with [USN:L6N4660DJ TEXT:"protesters demanding"] more money for underfunded public services at a time when borrowing costs have risen to their highest since 2022 on [USN:L6N4660FV TEXT:"the bond market"]. Here's how the budget battle could play out: BUDGET VOTE? The budget bill is being reviewed in the lower house of parliament, where it is having a rough ride. A vote on the taxation side of the bill was due on Tuesday, but has been pushed back to October 27 because a large number of amendments still need to be discussed. Budget Minister David Amiel has warned that amendments already approved would worsen the budget deficit by €10 billion ($11 billion). The constitution grants lawmakers 70 days to debate and amend it, first in the lower house and then in the Senate before it returns to the lower chamber for a final vote. However, the bill is unlikely to reach that point if opposition parties hold firm against Lecornu's plans for €54 billion in budget savings. That means the government will likely have to consider other options to pass the budget. RETURN OF ARTICLE 49.3? Since a 2024 snap legislative election produced a hung parliament, successive minority governments have leaned on Article 49.3 of the constitution to force through budgets without a vote. However, opposition parties can respond with threats of a no-confidence motion, forcing the government to make concessions — typically to Socialists, centrists or conservatives — to survive. With political parties already positioning for 2027, there may be little appetite to compromise this time. If a no-confidence vote is held and the government defeated following a 49.3, the budget bill would be dropped and the next cabinet forced back to the drawing board. SPECIAL ROLLOVER LAW If no budget passes after the 70 days, and the government doesn't invoke 49.3, it could pass an emergency law rolling over the 2026 budget until a proper one can be passed after the election. But the new president is expected to dissolve parliament and call fresh elections, meaning a full 2027 budget might not pass until well into the second half of the year, just as work begins on the 2028 budget. A finance ministry report warned such a rollover would cause unprecedented budget paralysis, freezing investment and planned defence-spending increases while welfare costs keep climbing. The deficit could widen by at least half a percentage point, denting investor confidence and pushing up borrowing costs, it said. BUDGET BY ORDINANCE If the government survives past mid-December without a budget law, it could try passing one by ordinance, bypassing parliament entirely on the state's most important annual legislation. This has never been done in the Fifth Republic, and legal experts view it as a nuclear option likely to trigger a no-confidence vote. Unlike the 49.3 route, the fall of a government afterwards wouldn't automatically void a budget passed by ordinance. Macron would likely struggle to install a new government before the election, however, leaving Lecornu's cabinet in a caretaker role. In practice, an ordinance budget would probably serve as a stopgap until a new government wins parliamentary backing for its own fiscal plan late in 2027. ($1 = 0.8916 euros)

item.description: Plus de 70 morts lors d'une attaque à la frontière entre Soudan et Soudan du Sud selon le ministre Yohana Akol Ngor
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Plus de 70 morts lors d'une attaque à la frontière entre Soudan et Soudan du Sud selon le ministre Yohana Akol Ngor NAIROBI, 20 octobre (Reuters) - Au moins 73 personnes ont été tuées par des frappes de drones sur un marché d'Abiyé, région riche en pétrole située à la frontière entre le Soudan du Sud et le Soudan et revendiquée par les deux pays, a déclaré mardi le ministre de l'Information par intérim de la région, accusant les forces de Khartoum. Pékin accuse la marine américaine d'incursion "illégale" en mer de Chine méridionale PÉKIN/TAIPEI, 20 octobre (Reuters) - - L'armée chinoise a annoncé mardi avoir déployé des forces navales après l'incursion "illégale" d'un navire de guerre américain dans des eaux territoriales disputées en mer de Chine méridionale. L'Alberta vote pour rester au sein du Canada CALGARY, Canada, 20 octobre (Reuters) - Les habitants de la province canadienne de l'Alberta, riche en pétrole, ont, sans surprise, voté en faveur du maintien au sein du Canada lors du tout premier référendum, qui était consultatif, sur une éventuelle indépendance. États-Unis: La cote de popularité de Trump à un nouveau plus bas historique selon un sondage Reuters/Ipsos WASHINGTON, 20 octobre (Reuters) - La cote de popularité du président Donald Trump est tombée à 31%, un nouveau plus bas historique depuis le début de sa carrière politique, les Américains se disant inquiets de la hausse des prix de l'essence et prêts à sanctionner le parti républicain lors des élections de mi-mandat du 3 novembre. Trump juge que Kyiv devrait écarter Zelensky des négociations 19 octobre (Reuters) - Le président américain Donald Trump a déclaré lundi qu'il estimait qu'une autre personne que le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky devrait négocier au nom de Kyiv dans le cadre des efforts visant à mettre fin à la guerre avec la Russie. Witkoff devrait se rendre en Norvège et en Russie pour des discussions sur l'Ukraine NEW YORK/WASHINGTON, 20 octobre (Reuters) - Steve Witkoff, l'émissaire spécial du président américain Donald Trump, devrait se rendre cette semaine en Norvège pour un nouveau cycle de pourparlers sur l'Ukraine et se déplacer également en Russie pour y rencontrer le président Vladimir Poutine, ont déclaré des personnes au fait de la question. Yémen-Cinquante-trois morts dans une attaque houthie contre un camp militaire gouvernemental 19 octobre (Reuters) - Cinquante-trois personnes ont été tuées lundi et 200 blessées dans une attaque des rebelles houthis, soutenus par l'Iran, contre un camp d'entraînement militaire du gouvernement yéménite dans la province de Chabwa, dans l'est du Yémen, selon des responsables gouvernementaux. Italie-Les boutiques de Milan ont fermé plus tôt, craintes de nouveaux pillages MILAN, 19 octobre (Reuters) - Les magasins du centre de Milan ont fermé plus tôt que d'habitude lundi et ont barricadé leurs vitrines, craignant de nouveaux troubles après deux jours de manifestations au cours desquels des groupes de personnes cagoulées se sont affrontés avec la police, ont pillé des magasins et saccagé des biens. Grèce: Douze migrants, dont un nourrisson, se noient dans deux naufrages au large des îles grecques 19 octobre (Reuters) - Douze migrants, dont un nourrisson, se sont noyés lundi lors de deux accidents différents au large des îles grecques de Lesbos et de Samos, dans le nord-est de la mer Égée, après le chavirement de leurs embarcations alors qu'elles étaient poursuivies par les garde-côtes, ont indiqué les autorités. Australie-Une députée dans un état critique après avoir été percutée délibérement par une voiture SYDNEY, 19 octobre (Reuters) - La députée australienne Helen Haines est dans un état critique après avoir été délibérément percutée lundi par une voiture devant son bureau, à Wangaratta, au nord-est de Melbourne.
